title.rendered: Apple launches Upgrade leasing for iPhone, Mac, iPad, and Apple Watch

content.rendered:
Apple has launched Apple Upgrade, a new Klarna-backed program that lets U.S. customers lease an iPhone, iPad, Mac, or Apple Watch. Monthly payments start at $11.99, but the customer does not own the device when the lease ends.

The program is available through Apple’s website, the Apple Store app, and U.S. Apple Stores. It also replaces new enrollments in the iPhone Upgrade Program and iPhone Payments.

How Apple Upgrade works

Customers select an eligible device and choose Apple Upgrade at checkout. Klarna then runs a soft credit check, which Apple says will not affect the applicant’s credit score. Once approved, payments and lease details are managed in the Klarna app.

The available terms and advertised starting prices depend on the product:

An existing device can be traded in when starting the lease, spreading its value across the monthly payments for the initial term. It is worth checking the trade-in value first, as that credit does not carry over to a lease extension or the next upgrade.

At the end of the term, customers have three choices:

  • Return the device and leave the program.
  • Return it and begin a new lease on another device.
  • Pay a one-time purchase option fee to keep it.

That final point is the main difference between leasing and buying with monthly installments. For example, Apple lists a 256GB iPhone 17 Pro at $31.99 a month for 24 months. Those payments total $767.76, but the phone still belongs to Klarna. Keeping it requires paying the remaining purchase amount.

Customers get six months after the initial term to decide. During that extension, monthly payments may rise. If no action is taken by the end of the six months, Klarna charges the purchase option fee.

AppleCare costs extra

AppleCare is not included in Apple Upgrade. Customers can add AppleCare+ or place the leased device on an AppleCare One plan, but Apple bills that coverage separately. Our AppleCare One and AppleCare+ comparison can help decide which option makes more sense.

The extra protection may matter more with a lease because the device must be returned in good working condition. Apple warns that damage fees may apply if it is lost, stolen, or returned in unacceptable condition.

Early upgrades and cancellations can also cost extra. After Apple’s 14-day return window, ending the lease early generally means paying all unpaid monthly lease payments through the end of the term.

Not every Apple device qualifies

Apple Upgrade covers the iPhone 17 lineup, MacBook Air, MacBook Pro, iMac, Mac Studio, iPad Pro, iPad Air, iPad mini, Apple Watch Series 11, and Apple Watch Ultra 3.

The iPhone 16 and 16 Plus, Apple Watch SE, MacBook Neo, Mac mini, entry-level iPad with A16, and Studio Display are excluded. Education, government, military, employee, and business store purchases are also ineligible.

Leasing an iPhone requires activation with AT&T, T-Mobile, or Verizon. Applicants must be U.S. residents, meet the age requirement in their state, and provide a Social Security number or ITIN.

Existing iPhone Upgrade Program members can keep making their current payments. When they become eligible for another iPhone, Apple will offer Apple Upgrade, Apple Card Monthly Installments, carrier financing, or an outright purchase instead of renewing the old plan.

Unlock more with Apple:

  • AirPods 5 Wireless Earbuds
  • Apple HomeView
  • Apple TV 4K (4th gen)
  • MacBook Neo 13-inch Laptop
  • iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)
  • MacBook Air 13-inch Laptop with M5 chip

As an Amazon Associate, iGeeksBlog earns from qualifying purchases.

title.rendered: Apple Smart Home Hub launch timeline narrowed in new report

content.rendered:
Apple’s long-rumored smart home hub is reportedly on track to launch sometime between October 2026 and early 2027, according to a new report from Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman.

Rather than releasing a single smart display, Apple is reportedly developing both tabletop and wall-mounted versions designed for different rooms throughout the home, with Siri serving as the primary way users interact with the device.

The smart home hub is expected to feature a 7-inch display paired with a HomePod-like speaker. Apple reportedly envisions it as a central smart home controller for everyday tasks, including managing HomeKit accessories, making FaceTime calls, viewing calendars, controlling media playback, and accessing information through Siri AI.

Apple is building the hub around Siri and smart home controls

According to the report, Apple plans to offer both tabletop and wall-mounted versions of the smart home hub, making it suitable for locations such as the kitchen, living room, bedroom, or hallway.

Instead of relying on a single shared display, Apple wants the device to fit naturally into different spaces around the home. Bloomberg reports that the company expects some households to purchase multiple hubs to create a connected smart home experience.

The report also says the device will run a new operating system based on tvOS. Its interface is expected to blend design elements from watchOS and iOS, featuring app icons, widgets, and customizable clock faces on the main screen.

FaceTime, HomeKit, and personalized experiences are expected

Apple is also reportedly working on personalized features for the smart home hub.

According to Bloomberg, the device will use facial recognition to identify the person standing in front of it and automatically surface relevant information, such as calendars, reminders, or personalized widgets. The interface is also expected to dynamically adjust the size of on-screen elements based on how close the user is to the display.

In addition to controlling HomeKit accessories, users are expected to be able to make FaceTime calls, play music, check calendars, browse photo galleries, and use the hub as an intercom between Apple devices throughout the home.

Bloomberg also reports that Apple is continuing development of an advanced indoor security camera designed to compete with products such as Amazon Ring, further expanding the company’s smart home ecosystem.

While Apple has yet to officially announce the smart home hub, the report suggests the company is moving closer to entering the rapidly growing smart home display market with a Siri-first experience.

Would you add Apple’s smart home hub to your smart home setup, or are you happy with your current devices? Let us know in the comments below.

title.rendered: Fortnite Festival Season 15: Lil Tecca skin and cosmetics revealed

content.rendered:
With Fortnite Festival Season 15 scheduled to kick off on July 30, Epic Games just announced Lil Tecca as its headlining artist. As usual, the American rapper will also be added to Fortnite’s growing celeb skins catalog along with pickaxes, jam tracks, and other relevant in-game items.

As the latest in a long list of musicians to have partnered with Fortnite, Lil Tecca joins some of the most popular stars of his industry, such as Eminem, Travis Scott, and Ice Spice. Moreover, while doing so, he is also set to succeed Season 14’s featured singer Laufey, who was added to the game in April 2026.

All Lil Tecca cosmetics in Fortnite Festival Season 15

Besides announcing Lil Tecca for the new season, Fortnite Festival devs also revealed a range of themed content that the forthcoming seasonal update will entail. This includes the all-new Festival Main Stage, the cosmetics obtained via Music Pass, and the cosmetics that will go up for sale in the Item Shop.

Firstly, Fortnite Festival will roll out the Neon Dreams Music Pass, which will offer players a string of in-game items. The Tour Ready Lil Tecca skin, Tecca’s World back bling, the Mic Mace pickaxe, and the Dopamine Tour-themed guitar are the rewards that can be unlocked by purchasing the pass.

Moreover, the Festival Main stage is also getting a reskin, with prominent influence drawn from Lil Tecca. There will be a total of 4 jam tracks for Fortnite users to play, featuring hits such as “Ransom”, “500lbs”, “Love Me”, and “Dark Thoughts”.

In addition to all that, the 23-year-old musician’s skin and other themed in-game items will also make their way to the Item Shop. The content in discussion involves the Lil Tecca skin, the We Love You Tecca-inspired Mic Stand, Dopamine Blades pickaxe, and the Dark Thoughts emote.

Wrapping up

Lil Tecca is apparently a major rapper among young audiences, and his arrival in Fortnite Festival, as the main attraction, will be welcome news for a significant section of the game’s players. At the same time, Epic Games will also hope that the collab will bring over a chunk of the “Ransom” rapper’s 17.3 million monthly listeners (accurate as of the time of writing) on Spotify. However, only time will tell how strong a reception this game mode receives upon his arrival.

title.rendered: How to get the IShowSpeed skin in Fortnite

content.rendered:
Internet celeb IShowSpeed has landed in Fortnite again, along with a bunch of different cosmetics inspired by him. Interestingly, the IShowSpeed skin was first introduced in December 2025 and has since entered the Item Shop on three different occasions already.

There are two skins modeled around the American streamer, which are IShowSpeed and ISuperSpeed. They are worth 1,500 V-Bucks and 1,200 V-Bucks, respectively. Importantly, these items are on sale for a limited time, until July 29, 2026, by 5 PM PT or 8 PM ET.

Steps to claim the IShowSpeed Fortnite skin

Besides purchasing any of these two skins individually, you can also get them both together, alongside themed in-game accessories, by purchasing the IShowSpeed Bundle worth 3,000 V-Bucks. Taking into account the total V-Bucks value of each item in the bundle, you save a whopping 3,600 V-Bucks by getting the bundle.

  1. In Fortnite, go to the Shop tab.
  2. Next, scroll down to the Icons category and, under the “IShowSpeed” section, select your preferred Speed skin.
  3. Finally, press and hold the Purchase button to complete the transaction.

All IShowSpeed cosmetics in Fortnite

1. Speed Cam (back bling)

Price: 300 V-Bucks
Also available in: IShowSpeed Bundle

2. Speed’s Trident (pickaxe)

Price: 800 V-Bucks
Also available in: IShowSpeed Bundle

3. IShow’s Speedboard (glider)

Price: 800 V-Bucks
Also available in: IShowSpeed Bundle

4. ISpeedStyle (wrap)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available in: IShowSpeed Bundle

5. ISuperSpeed’s Emblem (pack of back bling and pickaxe)

Price: 800 V-Bucks
Also available in: IShowSpeed Bundle

6. Barrier Breaker (emote)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available in: IShowSpeed Bundle

7. Head Shot / Gas In The Truck (jam track)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available in: IShowSpeed Bundle

Wrapping up

Fortnite has a knack for collaborating with celebs and, among them, IShowSpeed is certainly among the more popular ones when you consider the young age groups. Safe to say, with multiple different Item Shop appearances since his debut in the game, players have got enough opportunities to nab the YouTube personality’s cosmetics.

More recently, another notable streamer, Mongraal, made his own debut in Epic’s multiplayer title. Similar to his contemporaries, the Fortnite pro was added as a skin while other cosmetic items themed around him were also incorporated into the game. As such, Fortnite now has an impressive array of famous streamers in its skins catalog, which also includes the likes of Ninja, LoserFruit, and Kai Cenat.

  • How to get the Hoshimachi Suisei skin in Fortnite
  • How to get Squid Game skins in Fortnite

  • Razer Naga V3 Pro Gaming Mouse

title.rendered: I compared the best free calorie counter apps: These are the ones worth using

content.rendered:
Finding a genuinely free calorie counter app is harder than it should be. In my weight loss journey, I tested multiple apps that promise easy calorie counting, customized nutrition analysis, and even weight loss solutions. However, most of those good features were locked behind a paywall after a few days.

The good news? Not every app follows that pattern. After comparing the most popular calorie counter apps available for iPhone and Android, I found a handful offering enough free features to make daily calorie, nutrition, and macro tracking simple.

If you’re trying to lose weight, build muscle, or simply become more aware of your food intake, these are the free calorie tracker apps worth downloading.

How I tested these free calorie counter apps

To keep this comparison as fair as possible, I evaluated each app using the same testing criteria rather than relying on feature lists alone.

For each app, I downloaded the free version on my iPhone and Android and used it as my primary calorie tracker for a week for logging meals and drinks throughout the day.

I also tested features that matter most to people tracking calories:

  • Food database: How easy was it to find common foods and restaurant meals?
  • Barcode scanner: Did it work reliably, and was it included in the free version?
  • Meal logging: How many taps did it take to log a typical meal?
  • Macro tracking: Could I easily view protein, carbs, and fat without upgrading?
  • User experience: Was the interface clean and intuitive, or full of advertisements and upselling?
  • Health integrations: I checked whether the app could sync with Apple Health or Google Fit.
  • Premium limitations: I noted which features were genuinely free and which required a paid subscription.

I wasn’t looking for the app with the longest list of features. My goal was to find the ones that make calorie tracking fast, accurate, and easy enough that I’d actually want to use them every day. After all, the best calorie counter app isn’t the one with the flashiest dashboard—it’s the one you’ll stick with consistently.

Best calorie counter apps on iPhone and Android I’d recommend

1. Calorie Counter – MyNetDiary: Completely ad-free experience

MyNetDiary tops my list as it offers calorie counter, barcode scanning, macro tracking, progress charts, customizable dashboard, and even nutrient analysis—all without ads. That’s surprisingly rare among calorie counter apps today. I can even share my food diary with my dietitian or health coach.

Another thing that makes MyNetDiary different is its focus on accuracy. Instead of relying heavily on user-submitted food entries, I can log meals from its staff-verified food database with more than 2 million foods. If you care about macro tracking, you’ll also appreciate its detailed nutrition breakdown, covering vitamins, fiber, protein, and 105+ other nutrients.

While the free version is one of the strongest I’ve compared, some advanced features, including AI meal scanning, personalized diet plans, GLP-1 companion, intermittent fasting tools, health tracking, and wearable integrations, are reserved for Premium. Still, for most people, the free version goes much further than many competing apps.

Key features

  • Free calorie and nutrition counter with no ads
  • Highly accurate staff-verified database with over 2 million food items
  • Water intake, exercise, and weight tracking
  • Progress charts and customizable nutrition goals
  • Meal reminders and shopping lists

Pros

  • One of the most generous free calorie counter apps
  • Fast and intuitive meal logging
  • Excellent macro and micronutrient tracking
  • Great for weight loss, fitness, and long-term nutrition tracking

Cons

  • Some premium tools, like AI coaching and meal plans, require a subscription
  • The interface is more functional than modern-looking
  • The large number of nutrition metrics may feel overwhelming for beginners

Best For: Anyone looking for a powerful free calorie counter app with accurate nutrition data, zero ads, and enough features to track calories and macros without feeling pressured to upgrade.

Download: iPhone | Android

2. MyFitnessPal: Get the largest food database for quick logging

MyFitnessPal has been one of the biggest names in calorie tracking for years, and it’s easy to see why. Even with several popular features moving behind a Premium subscription, the free version is still one of the easiest ways to track calories thanks to its massive food database and quick meal logging.

Whether I am eating homemade meals, restaurant dishes, or packaged snacks, most of the time I find them by searching. And my favorite meals are already saved for quick logging. The app also lets you monitor your daily calorie intake, view macronutrients, set calorie goals, track weight and exercise, and sync data with compatible health and fitness apps.

For someone who simply wants to build a consistent food logging habit, that’s more than enough. However, I find the free version limiting as it has the basic barcode scanning locked behind a subscription. Moreover, meal scan, intermittent fasting, and advanced nutrition features all require a Premium subscription.

Key features

  • Access to one of the world’s largest food databases with over 20 million foods
  • Log meals, snacks, water, and exercise
  • Set calorie and macro goals by percentage
  • Record weight and body measurements
  • View nutrition progress and daily summaries
  • Sync with 40+ health platforms and fitness apps

Pros

  • Huge food database makes finding foods quick and easy
  • Easy-to-use interface that’s beginner-friendly
  • Create and save custom meals and recipes
  • Great choice for building a consistent calorie-tracking habit

Cons

  • Barcode scanner, advanced nutrition analysis and AI tools require a Premium subscription
  • Frequent prompts encouraging users to upgrade
  • Free version includes ads

Best For: People who want a straightforward way to log meals every day. However, the free version requires you to search for foods manually for calorie counting and macro tracking.

Download: iPhone | Android

3. Cronometer – Best app for detailed nutrition and macro tracking

If you’re the type of person who wants to track more than just calories, Cronometer is hard to beat. While most of the calorie counter apps concentrate only on calories and macros, Cronometer offers me a very detailed nutrient profile including protein, carbs, fat, fiber, vitamins, minerals, and more than 95 nutrients and compounds.

What really sets Cronometer apart is how generous its free version is. You get access to a curated database of over 1.1 million verified foods, unlimited barcode scanning, custom recipes, exercise tracking, and integration with fitness apps. That makes it one of the best free yet accurate calorie counter apps for anyone serious about improving their diet.

The trade-off is that Cronometer isn’t as beginner-friendly as apps like MyFitnessPal. The wealth of nutrition data can feel overwhelming if all you want to do is count calories. Advanced features like AI photo logging, recipe importing, fasting tools, long-term reports, and an ad-free experience are also reserved for the Gold subscription.

Key features

  • Track calories, protein, carbs, fat, fiber, and 95+ nutrients and compounds
  • Curated database with over 1.1 million verified food entries
  • Unlimited free barcode scanner
  • Track weight, exercise, water intake, and other health metrics
  • Customize calorie and nutrition targets
  • Sync with Apple Health, Fitbit, Garmin, Oura, WHOOP, and other supported apps and devices

Pros

  • One of the most feature-rich free calorie counter apps
  • Unlimited barcode scanning at no extra cost
  • Supports a wide range of health apps and fitness wearables

Cons

  • The interface can feel data-heavy for first-time users
  • Free version includes ads

Best For: Health-conscious users, athletes, and anyone who wants weight loss, muscle gain, and overall nutrition improvements.

Download: iPhone | Android

4. Calorie Counter by fatsecret – Free barcode scanner

Most calorie counter apps start out free but quickly remind you that the best features come with a subscription. FatSecret takes a different approach. It gives you access to calorie tracking, a barcode scanner, macro tracking, and weight logging without forcing you to upgrade.

What I like most about FatSecret is that it sticks to the basics and does them well. The home screen isn’t packed with AI coaches, meal plans, or flashy wellness scores. Instead, you get a straightforward food diary, a large food database, an exercise log, and progress charts that make it easy to see how you’re doing over time.

Key features

  • Free calorie, carb, protein, and fat tracking
  • Barcode scanner included at no extra cost
  • Exercise diary and calorie burn tracking
  • Recipe library and meal ideas
  • Syncs with Apple Health, Fitbit, and Google Fit

Pros

  • Most core features are available for free
  • Barcode scanner doesn’t require a Premium subscription
  • Simple and distraction-free food logging
  • Fewer upgrade prompts than many competing apps

Cons

  • Outdated design compared to newer calorie trackers
  • Premium is required for meal planning and some advanced insights
  • Smaller community and fewer smart features than apps like MyFitnessPal

Best For: Anyone who wants a no-nonsense calorie counter that prioritizes useful free features over constant upselling.

Download: iPhone | Android

5. Lose It! – Best for beginners

Lose It! is one of the easiest calorie counter apps I will recommend if you’ve never tracked calories before. From the moment I opened the app, it guided me to set a weight-loss goal and calculate my daily calorie budget based on my body composition, activity levels, and habits.

The clean design and intuitive interface make it beginner-friendly. You can log meals and exercise, track your daily calorie intake, monitor your weight, create custom foods, and view your daily progress. These features will be enough for most people who count their calories to stay within the daily calorie allowance.

Where Lose It! falls behind some competitors is its Premium paywall. Features like the barcode scanner, AI photo and voice logging, advanced macro tracking, intermittent fasting, and detailed nutrition insights require a paid subscription.

Key features

  • Personalized daily calorie budget based on your goals
  • Track daily calorie consumption and weight progress
  • Save favorite foods, meals, and recipes for faster logging
  • Basic tracking for calories and macronutrients
  • Support groups to stay motivated

Pros

  • Beginner-friendly interface that’s easy to navigate
  • Quick and simple calorie logging
  • Personalized calorie goals help keep you on track

Cons

  • Free version has basic macro and nutrition tracking
  • Barcode scanner, AI meal logging and advanced nutrition tools are Premium-only for new users
  • Lots of ads and regular upgrade prompts

Best For: Beginners who want a simple, motivating calorie tracker without a steep learning curve.

Download: iPhone | Android

Which calorie counter app I would actually keep using

After comparing these apps side by side, one thing became clear: not all “free” calorie counter apps are equally free. Some let you track calories without restrictions, while others lock everyday features like barcode scanning or detailed nutrition behind a subscription.

Here’s how they compare in terms of the features available for you without any payment.

  • Best overall free app: MyNetDairy
  • Biggest food database: MyFitnessPal
  • Beginner-friendly: Lose It!
  • Best for nutrition tracking: Cronometer
  • Free barcode scanning: fatsecret

If I were judging purely on free features, Cronometer takes the top spot. It gives you access to unlimited barcode scanning, detailed nutrient tracking, custom recipes, and one of the most accurate food databases without asking you to upgrade immediately.

That said, FatSecret deserves a close second. It may not have the flashiest interface, but it’s one of the few apps that still treats the free version like a complete product instead of a demo.

Tips for choosing the right calorie counter app

Before you download the first app you see, think about how you plan to use it. The right choice depends more on your goals than the number of features it offers.

  • Decide what you’re tracking: If your goal is staying within a calorie budget, any app will work. However, if I monitor protein intake, try improving your nutrition, and track vitamins and minerals, an app like MyNetDairy is better.
  • Check which features are actually free: Many apps advertise barcode scanning, fasting tools, or AI food recognition, but these often require a paid subscription. Try it to see what you can actually use without paying.
  • Pick an app you’ll enjoy using: You’ll probably log meals multiple times a day. If the interface feels cluttered or confusing, you’re less likely to stick with it.
  • Look for Apple Health or Google Fit integration: It’s non-negotiable for me. Syncing your activity automatically can save time and make calorie tracking more accurate.
  • Don’t feel pressured to upgrade: Most people don’t need AI meal plans, coaching programs, or premium recipes. Try the free version for a few weeks before deciding whether a subscription is actually worth it.

Final verdict

Free calorie counter apps have improved significantly over the past few years, but they aren’t all created equal. Some are generous enough to allow you to track calories without making you pay anything, while others keep their basic functions reserved for their paid users.

If you’re looking for the best overall free calorie counter, Cronometer is my top recommendation. It offers the strongest combination of calorie tracking, macro and micronutrient analysis, barcode scanning, and an accurate food database in its free plan.

In the end, none of the calorie counter apps can ever replace consistency. The one that helps you develop the habit of entering all your food entries will be far more useful than one with hundreds of premium features you won’t use. Start with a free option, see which one fits your routine, and only consider upgrading if you genuinely need the extra tools.

title.rendered: This Chrome feature saves your favorite AI prompts so you can reuse them

content.rendered:
If you use AI every day, you’ve probably realized the biggest time sink isn’t waiting for responses. It’s typing the same prompts again and again.

Whether you’re asking Gemini to summarize articles, rewrite emails, extract action items, or simplify technical content, chances are you’ve reused the same instructions dozens of times. Google Chrome now has a feature that solves exactly that problem.

The browser’s Skills feature lets you save your best AI prompts and reuse them whenever you need them. Instead of copying prompts from a notes app or searching through old conversations, you can trigger them directly from Chrome’s Gemini side panel with just a few keystrokes.

Here’s everything you need to know about Google Chrome Skills and how to start using them.

What are Google Chrome Skills?

If you’ve ever found yourself typing the same Gemini prompt every morning, Chrome Skills was built for exactly that. Whether it’s asking Gemini to summarize a webpage, clean up an email, or pull action items from a document, you can save those instructions once and reuse them whenever you need them.

Saved prompts appear inside Chrome’s Gemini side panel, so you don’t have to dig through old chats or keep a document full of prompt templates. Just launch the Skill, and Gemini runs the same instructions again on the page you’re viewing or the content you’ve pasted.

Why Google Chrome Skills are worth setting up

If Gemini is already part of your workflow, Chrome Skills can save a surprising amount of repetitive work.

Here are a few reasons why it’s worth using:

  • No need to type the same prompts repeatedly: Save frequently used instructions and access them in seconds.
  • Keep your best prompts in one place: You don’t have to search through old chats or maintain a separate notes document.
  • Works with the webpage you’re viewing: Many Skills can use the current tab as context, making tasks like summarizing articles or extracting information much quicker.
  • Works across multiple tabs: Compare products, research different sources, or analyze several webpages without constantly copying and pasting text.
  • Consistent results: Since you’re using the same prompt every time, you get more predictable outputs for recurring tasks.

How to save AI prompts as Chrome Skills

Saving a prompt as a Skill only takes a few clicks:

  1. Open the webpage you want in Google Chrome and click the Ask Gemini button in the top right corner.
  2. Here, type the prompt you want to reuse.
  3. Let Gemini generate a response.
  4. Now, hover over your original prompt and click the lightning bolt icon that appears beside it.
  5. Next, give your Skill a name and click Save. You can also edit the prompt or add extra instructions before saving it.

The saved prompt is now available whenever you need it.

How to use saved Chrome Skills

Using a saved Skill is even easier than creating one.

  1. Open any web page and click the Ask Gemini button in the top-right corner.
    Open the webpage you want in Google Chrome and click the Ask Gemini button in the top-right corner.
  2. Here, type a / (forward slash) and select one of your saved Skills from the contextual menu that appears.
  3. You can also click the + button and select one of your saved Skills.
  4. Press Enter.

Once done, Chrome will automatically insert the saved prompt and run it.

Best AI prompts worth saving as Skills

Not every prompt deserves to become a Skill. The best ones are the tasks you perform repeatedly.

Summarize long articles

Summarize the main argument of this webpage in one short paragraph, followed by three key takeaways in bullet points. Focus only on the essential facts.

This works well for news articles, research papers, documentation, and lengthy blog posts.

Polish emails

Rewrite this email to improve grammar, clarity, and flow while keeping it professional, polite, and concise.

Perfect for replying to clients, coworkers, or recruiters without spending extra time polishing every message.

Extract tasks and deadlines

Read this document and identify all action items, deadlines, responsibilities, and deliverables. Present everything as a checklist.

Useful for meeting notes, project briefs, contracts, and shared documents.

Explain complex topics

Explain this topic in simple language using everyday examples. Avoid technical jargon.

Ideal when you’re reading documentation or learning something unfamiliar.

Make complex content easier to understand

Rewrite this content so someone with no background knowledge can easily understand it. Keep sentences short and conversational.

Helpful for educators, technical writers, marketers, and content creators.

Things to keep in mind

If you can’t find Chrome Skills yet, check these requirements:

  • Update Google Chrome to the latest version.
  • Turn on Gemini in Chrome Settings.
  • Set Chrome’s language to English (U.S.).
  • Save Skills using the Google account you regularly work with.

Also remember that Skills are tied to Chrome’s Gemini integration. They won’t automatically work inside ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, or other AI assistants.

Who should use Chrome Skills?

Chrome Skills is useful for anyone who regularly uses Gemini in Chrome, especially if you find yourself repeating the same prompts throughout the day.

  • Writers and editors: Save prompts for proofreading, rewriting, summarizing articles, or generating headlines.
  • Students: Create Skills to explain complex topics, summarize research papers, or turn lengthy notes into quick study guides.
  • Developers: Reuse prompts for reviewing code, explaining error messages, generating documentation, or debugging snippets.
  • Researchers: Save prompts that extract key findings, compare multiple sources, or summarize long reports.
  • Marketing professionals: Speed up tasks like writing social media posts, improving ad copy, brainstorming ideas, or creating content briefs.
  • Business users: Use Skills to summarize meeting notes, identify action items, rewrite emails, and organize information from documents.

Even if you don’t fit into one of these categories, Chrome Skills can save time whenever you rely on the same Gemini prompts again and again.

Save time with Chrome Skills

Chrome Skills doesn’t look like a major feature at first, but it can save a lot of time if you regularly use Gemini. Once your favorite prompts are saved, you can reuse them in seconds instead of typing them from scratch every time.

What’s the one AI prompt you use every day? Share it in the comments below.

aioseo_head_json.author_bio:
Vikhyat has a bachelor’s degree in Electronic and Communication Engineering and over five years of writing experience. His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. 

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: Peacemaker skin returns to Fortnite: Here’s how to get it

content.rendered:
After a hiatus of around 300 days, the Peacemaker skin, based on the namesake 2022 series, and its associated cosmetics are once again up for grabs in Fortnite. As part of the latest promo, Aquaman nemesis Manta and Arrowverse superhero Dreamer have also joined the online multiplayer title.

Peacemaker first arrived in Fortnite back in September 2025 during Chapter 6 Season 4. In its latest run, the skin is available to claim until July 29, 2026, by 5 PM PT or 8 PM ET, which is also the deadline for claiming the Manta and Dreamer outfits. While Peacemaker and Dreamer skins are priced at 1,200 V-Bucks, the Manta skin is selling for 1,500 V-Bucks.

Steps to claim Peacemaker skin in Fortnite

  1. In Fortnite, navigate to the Shop tab.
  2. Scroll down to the “DC” section and select the Peacemaker skin.
  3. Press and hold the Purchase button to confirm your decision.

Alternatively, you can buy the DC anti-hero’s skin, along with his other in-game gear, via the Peacemaker bundle priced at 2,000 V-Bucks. Doing this would cost you 1,300 V-Bucks less than buying each of those items separately.

Other DC cosmetics recently added to Fortnite

1. Eagly (back bling)

Price: 400 V-Bucks
Also available in: Peacemaker Bundle

2. Peacemaker’s Shield (pickaxe)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available in: Peacemaker Bundle

3. Black Manta

Throughout the Fortnite Runners season, a variety of DC superheroes and supervillains have been rotated in the Item Shop. title.rendered: Amazon proposes 5,105-satellite network that could boost iPhone satellite services

content.rendered:
Amazon has proposed deploying 5,105 low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites as part of a new direct-to-device mobile network. According to a filing with the Federal Communications Commission (FCC), the constellation is designed to let compatible smartphones access voice calls, messaging, mobile data, and emergency services in areas without traditional cellular coverage.

If approved, the network could also strengthen Apple’s satellite ecosystem through Amazon’s planned acquisition of Globalstar, although neither company has announced any changes to existing iPhone satellite features.

The network is designed to expand coverage in remote areas

According to the FCC filing, Amazon plans to divide the constellation into five orbital shells.

The company says three shells will primarily serve regions with the highest population density, while the remaining two shells will focus on improving coverage across higher latitudes, including remote and polar regions where reliable connectivity is often limited.

Amazon says compatible smartphones will be able to access voice calling, messaging, mobile data, and emergency services over the satellite network without relying on traditional cellular towers.

The company also plans to integrate the new constellation with Globalstar, the satellite operator it is currently in the process of acquiring. If regulators approve the acquisition, Globalstar’s existing satellites and ground infrastructure will become part of Amazon’s broader direct-to-device satellite network.

Apple’s satellite services could benefit

Apple already relies on Globalstar’s satellite network to power several iPhone features, including Emergency SOS via Satellite, Messages via Satellite, Find My via Satellite, and Roadside Assistance via Satellite in supported countries and regions.

If Amazon completes its acquisition of Globalstar and successfully deploys its planned 5,105-satellite constellation, it could significantly expand the satellite infrastructure supporting those services in the future.

However, neither Amazon nor Apple has announced any plans to expand or modify Apple’s existing satellite features, and there is no confirmation that iPhone services will immediately benefit from the proposed network.

The proposal still requires approval from the FCC, while Amazon’s acquisition of Globalstar remains subject to regulatory review and is currently expected to close in 2027.

If both the acquisition and the satellite deployment move forward on schedule, Amazon could begin launching the first satellites in 2028, laying the foundation for a much larger direct-to-device satellite network.

Would you like future smartphones to support full satellite calling and mobile data whenever you’re outside cellular coverage? Let us know in the comments below.

  • Apple HomeView

title.rendered: This hidden trick lets you lock WhatsApp Web with a password

content.rendered:
I always assumed locking my laptop whenever I stepped away was enough to keep my WhatsApp conversations secure. But then I started thinking about all the situations where that isn’t practical. Maybe someone asks to use my computer, I need to share my screen during a meeting, or I simply leave my laptop unlocked for a few minutes. In any of those cases, opening WhatsApp Web takes only a click—no phone required.

While digging through WhatsApp’s settings, I discovered a feature I hadn’t noticed before. WhatsApp Web can now be protected with its own password. Not your Windows password or your Mac login, but a separate password that blocks anyone from opening your chats even if they already have access to your browser.

In this guide, I’ll show you how to lock WhatsApp Web with a password, explain how the feature works, and also walk you through enabling App Lock on Android, iPhone, and your computer for even better protection.

Why you should lock WhatsApp Web

Most people think about securing their phone.

Very few think about securing their browser.

If you’ve used WhatsApp Web before, chances are you’re still signed in. By design, WhatsApp continues syncing with linked devices until you manually sign out. It’s convenient—but it’s also a potential security risk.

Anyone who gains access to your browser could potentially:

  • Read your private conversations.
  • View shared photos and videos.
  • Send messages from your account.
  • Access work-related chats.
  • See confidential client information.

I realized that my browser had quietly become the weakest link in my WhatsApp security. Thankfully, WhatsApp has finally addressed that problem with its built-in App Lock feature.

What is WhatsApp app lock?

App Lock adds an extra password directly to your WhatsApp Web session, as well as the WhatsApp app on supported devices.

Instead of opening straight into your conversations, anyone trying to access WhatsApp first sees a password prompt. Until the correct password is entered, your chats remain hidden. WhatsApp also stops displaying new message notifications while the session is locked.

What impressed me most is that the password works independently of your computer’s login credentials. It protects only your WhatsApp Web session, so even if someone already has access to your browser, they still can’t open your chats.

One important thing to remember is that this password isn’t permanent across browser sessions. If you log out of WhatsApp Web, you’ll need to create a new App Lock password the next time you link your account.

Before WhatsApp introduced this feature, I experimented with browser extensions that claimed to password-protect WhatsApp Web. Eventually, I removed them all. Most required permission to read and modify webpages, injected their own scripts, and depended entirely on third-party developers. That never felt like the safest solution.

Using WhatsApp’s built-in App Lock is much easier and considerably more trustworthy.

How to lock WhatsApp Web with a password

Setting up App Lock takes less than a minute.

  1. Visit web.whatsapp.com and link your mobile if you haven’t already.
    Open WhatsApp on your mobile, tap the three-dot on Android or your profile picture on iPhone, select Linked devices, and scan the QR code on your browser screen.
  2. Click the three-dot icon at the top. You’ll now see a new option called App lock. Select it.
  3. Toggle on Enable app lock.
  4. WhatsApp will ask you to create a password. The password can contain 6 to 128 characters. Enter a unique combination of letters, numbers, and special characters that you don’t use elsewhere.
  5. Retype the password and click OK.
  6. Wait until it loads and click Done.
  7. You can decide when WhatsApp Web should lock itself. Inactivity options include:
    • After 1 minute
    • After 15 minutes
    • After 1 hour
    • After 8 hours
  8. Now, use WhatsApp Web as usual. When you need to leave your computer unattended, click the three-dot icon and select Lock app. Your chats disappear instantly until the password is entered.

For auto-lock, I personally use 1 minute. Yes, it’s slightly annoying, but privacy usually beats convenience.

As an extra layer of protection, you can also lock individual WhatsApp chats. That way, even if someone somehow gets past your WhatsApp Web password, they still won’t be able to open your most sensitive conversations.

What happens if you forget your WhatsApp Web password?

If you forget your WhatsApp Web App Lock password, don’t worry; you won’t lose your account or any of your chats.

The password protects only your current WhatsApp Web session. It isn’t connected to your WhatsApp account, your phone’s screen lock, your two-step verification PIN, or your device password.

To reset it:

  1. Go to WhatsApp Web. It will show you the password page. Click Log out at the bottom.
  2. WhatsApp will sign you out and display the sign-in QR code. Use your mobile to link it again.
  3. Create a new App Lock password using the same method.

Just keep in mind that this password isn’t the same as your phone’s screen lock, WhatsApp PIN, or two-step verification code. This is an additional layer of security, and resetting it will not affect your chats.

How to enable WhatsApp app lock on Android

Locking WhatsApp Web is a great first step, but it’s just as important to protect the WhatsApp app on your Android phone. If someone gets hold of your unlocked device, App Lock adds another layer of security before they can access your conversations.

Here’s how to enable it:

  1. Open WhatsApp on your Android phone.
  2. Tap the three-dot menu in the top-right corner and select Settings.
  3. Go to Privacy.
  4. Scroll down and tap App lock.
  5. Toggle on Unlock with biometric.
  6. Authenticate with your fingerprint or device credentials.
  7. Choose when WhatsApp should automatically lock.

I also recommend turning off Show content in notifications. That way, incoming message previews stay hidden whenever WhatsApp is locked.

How to enable WhatsApp app lock on iPhone

If you use WhatsApp on an iPhone, you can secure the app with Face ID or Touch ID, depending on your device.

Here’s how I set it up:

  1. Open WhatsApp and tap the Profile tab at the bottom to go to settings.
  2. Tap Privacy.
  3. Choose App Lock.
  4. Enable Require Face ID or Touch ID depending on your model.
  5. Select your preferred lock delay. I chose Immediately.

Once enabled, Face ID unlocks WhatsApp almost instantly, making it feel seamless while keeping your conversations protected.

Bonus: If you’re using iOS 18 and later, Apple also lets you lock individual apps. Touch and hold the WhatsApp icon on your Home Screen or App Library. Now, tap Require Face ID and confirm with Face ID or your passcode. This adds another layer of protection, even before WhatsApp itself opens.

Can you lock the WhatsApp desktop app?

This is where things get a little confusing.

Although WhatsApp Web and the desktop app look very similar, they don’t offer exactly the same features.

The built-in App Lock feature is currently available for the WhatsApp app on Windows. If you don’t see it yet, make sure you’re using the latest version of the app, as the feature may still be rolling out.

Unfortunately, the WhatsApp app for macOS doesn’t currently support App Lock, so Mac users will need to rely on macOS login security and other privacy features for now.

Three WhatsApp privacy tips I use

After enabling App Lock, I made a few other changes that significantly improved my WhatsApp privacy.

  • I lock WhatsApp manually before leaving my desk even for 30 seconds. It has an auto-lock feature, but I prefer immediate protection.
  • Always review active sessions. Every few weeks, I check the Linked Devices list in WhatsApp. If I see an unfamiliar browser or old computer, I log it out immediately.
  • Never use “Keep Me Signed In” on shared computers. I make sure to manually log out of WhatsApp from every browser after its purpose is served.

Keep your WhatsApp chats safe!

Most of us spend time securing our phones with Face ID, fingerprints, and strong passcodes, yet leave WhatsApp Web permanently signed in on our browser. That’s often the weakest point in our privacy.

If you regularly use WhatsApp Web, enabling App Lock takes less than a minute and adds an extra barrier between your conversations and anyone who has access to your computer. It’s especially worthwhile if you use a shared, office, or family PC.

I now consider it one of the first privacy settings every WhatsApp user should enable. Combined with biometric App Lock on your phone and regular reviews of your linked devices, it makes unauthorized access much less likely.

If you haven’t turned it on yet, now is a good time to do it. Your chats and your privacy are worth the extra few seconds.

title.rendered: Apple releases iOS 26.6 with security fixes, Spotlight improvements, and more

content.rendered:
Apple has released iOS 26.6 for all compatible iPhone models. Unlike iOS 26.4 and iOS 26.5, the latest update doesn’t introduce any major user-facing features. Instead, it focuses on delivering more than 75 security fixes, several quality-of-life improvements, and a number of behind-the-scenes enhancements that prepare iPhones for iOS 27.

The update is available now by going to Settings → General → Software Update. As always, Apple recommends installing the latest version to ensure your iPhone is protected with the newest security patches and system improvements.

Apple is preparing Spotlight for iOS 27

One of the most significant changes in iOS 26.6 happens behind the scenes.

Apple says the update optimizes the iPhone’s Spotlight index ahead of iOS 27, which significantly expands Spotlight’s role throughout the operating system with more powerful search capabilities and deeper Siri integration.

The optimization should also make upgrading to iOS 27 smoother. During the early beta period, some users noticed Spotlight continued indexing content for several days after installing the update. By completing part of that indexing work in iOS 26.6, Apple can reduce the amount of processing required after users upgrade to iOS 27 later this fall.

Reaching the blocked contacts limit is now easier to understand

Until now, iOS offered little explanation when users reached the maximum number of blocked contacts.

Attempting to block another phone number simply failed without clearly explaining why.

iOS 26.6 addresses this issue by introducing a new “Blocked Contacts Limit Reached” alert. Instead of silently failing, iOS now informs users that they’ve reached the limit and prompts them to remove an existing blocked contact before adding a new one.

Apple’s Anti-Snatching Protection isn’t ready yet

Although it isn’t included in today’s release, the iOS 26.6 beta revealed that Apple is still actively developing an Anti-Snatching Protection feature.

Code discovered during beta testing suggests the iPhone could detect when an unlocked device is suddenly snatched from its owner and automatically lock itself to prevent unauthorized access.

Apple has not announced when the feature will be released, and it remains disabled in the public version of iOS 26.6. For now, the beta code simply confirms that development is ongoing.

More than 75 security vulnerabilities have been patched

The biggest reason to install iOS 26.6 is security.

Apple has published details for more than 75 security fixes affecting iPhone and iPad, addressing vulnerabilities across multiple components of iOS and iPadOS.

Enterprise users also receive an important fix for an issue involving the DisableAssociationMACRandomization policy. According to Apple, the update resolves a bug that previously allowed users to modify the Private Wi-Fi Address setting even when IT administrators had restricted access through device management policies.

iOS 27 is the next major update

With iOS 26.6 now available, Apple’s focus is shifting toward iOS 27.

The next major iPhone software update is already available through the Developer Beta and Public Beta programs, with the stable release expected later this September.

If you don’t plan to install a beta version, iOS 26.6 is the best way to keep your iPhone secure and up to date while waiting for iOS 27. Although it isn’t packed with new features, it delivers important security improvements, resolves several usability issues, and lays the foundation for Apple’s next major software release.

Have you installed iOS 26.6 yet? Let us know if you’ve noticed any improvements or changes on your iPhone in the comments below.

Unlock more with Apple:

  • AirPods 5 Wireless Earbuds
  • Apple HomeView
  • Apple TV 4K (4th gen)
  • MacBook Neo 13-inch Laptop
  • iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)
  • MacBook Air 13-inch Laptop with M5 chip

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. title.rendered: YouTube Premium will add Peacock in the US in early 2027

content.rendered:
YouTube Premium is becoming a broader entertainment bundle. Starting in early 2027, eligible subscribers in the U.S. will gain access to Peacock Premium, according to YouTube’s announcement.

The included plan is Peacock’s ad-supported Premium tier, which currently costs $10.99 per month on its own. It adds NBC and Bravo shows, Universal movies, Peacock originals, and live sports to a membership already built around ad-free YouTube, downloads, background play, and YouTube Music.

Peacock will live inside YouTube

Subscribers will be able to watch Peacock within the YouTube experience. The catalog includes The Office, Saturday Night Live, Love Island USA, Law & Order: SVU, and The Traitors, along with sports from the NFL, NBA, MLB, Olympics, Premier League, WNBA, and more.

There is one important distinction: Peacock Premium still shows ads. YouTube says subscribers will also get an option to upgrade their Peacock membership, but it has not shared the upgrade price or other plan details.

YouTube is using the word “eligible,” so it is not yet clear whether every Premium plan or account will qualify. The company also has not announced a precise launch date, activation steps, or the final price of the combined membership. More details are due over the coming months.

YouTube keeps adding reasons to pay for Premium

YouTube has recently added podcast-focused features for Premium users, including simpler listening controls and automatic playback-speed adjustments. At the same time, it is making Picture-in-Picture available to more free users for long-form, non-music videos.

Adding an entire streaming service gives the paid plan a clearer advantage. NBCUniversal calls it Peacock’s largest wholesale distribution deal to date, potentially placing the service in front of millions of existing YouTube Premium members.

Peacock already has a discounted bundle with Apple TV. The YouTube deal goes further by putting Peacock content directly inside a service many people already use every day, though its value will depend on the price YouTube announces for 2027.

The partnership also extends NBCUniversal’s distribution agreement with YouTube TV. Separately, Peacock Premium will become a paid add-on through YouTube Primetime Channels later this summer, while Peacock Premium Plus is already available there.

Unlock more with Apple:

  • AirPods 5 Wireless Earbuds
  • Apple HomeView
  • Apple TV 4K (4th gen)
  • MacBook Neo 13-inch Laptop
  • iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)
  • MacBook Air 13-inch Laptop with M5 chip

title.rendered: Kimi K3’s open weights are here, but your Mac probably can’t run them

content.rendered:
Moonshot AI has released the full Kimi K3 model weights, opening its flagship AI model to downloads, private deployment, and fine-tuning. The release fulfills the company’s promise to publish the weights by July 27.

K3 is also appearing in third-party AI tools, but there is an important catch. Ollama currently offers it through the cloud, while LM Studio does not yet list an official K3 build. This is not a model most people can download and run on a MacBook.

The full model is about 1.56 TB

Kimi K3 has 2.8 trillion total parameters and activates 104 billion of them for each token. It supports text and images, has a 1-million-token context window, and uses a Mixture-of-Experts design that selects 16 of its 896 experts at a time.

Even with native MXFP4 compression, the official Hugging Face repository takes up roughly 1.56 TB. Moonshot’s deployment guidance recommends vLLM, SGLang, or TokenSpeed and a supernode with at least 64 accelerators.

That puts K3 in a completely different class from the smaller models people normally run locally on a Mac. Open weights make the model inspectable and self-hostable for well-equipped teams; they do not make it laptop-friendly.

Ollama access runs in the cloud

Ollama now lists kimi-k3:cloud, so users can launch the model from the familiar Ollama command line. However, the inference happens on Ollama’s servers rather than the user’s computer.

The listing currently requires an Ollama Pro or Max subscription and consumes extra usage credits. Ollama says it is adding capacity, which suggests access may remain constrained during the initial rollout.

LM Studio’s public model catalog does not show an official Kimi K3 build at the time of writing. Community conversions may appear, but K3’s size and new architecture mean finding a model in a catalog is not the same as being able to run it locally.

For comparison, models such as gpt-oss-20B can run offline on a suitably equipped Apple silicon Mac, while Gemma 4 includes models built for consumer hardware. K3 is aimed at data-center-scale deployment.

The license allows broad reuse, with conditions

The custom Kimi K3 License allows people and companies to use, modify, fine-tune, distribute, sublicense, and sell copies or derivatives of the model.

It adds extra conditions for large model-as-a-service businesses and commercial products with more than 100 million monthly users or over $20 million in monthly revenue. Those details matter more to AI providers than to researchers experimenting with the weights.

The release should make independent testing and private deployments possible for organizations with enough hardware. For everyone else, Ollama Cloud, Kimi’s own apps, and hosted APIs remain the practical ways to try K3.

  • Apple HomeView
  • Apple TV 4K (4th gen)
  • MacBook Neo 13-inch Laptop
  • iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)
  • MacBook Air 13-inch Laptop with M5 chip

title.rendered: The Lightest PDF editors for Windows I found (Ranked by tested)

content.rendered:
Search “lightweight PDF editor Windows,” and you’ll find a dozen listicles that are really just readers wearing an editor’s name tag. That’s a problem if you need to fix a typo, replace a logo, or fill out a form. I installed five tools that all claim to be lightweight PDF editors, timed them, monitored Task Manager, and opened the same stress-test files in each.

This review explains how I scored them and why “lightweight” and “just a viewer” get confused so often. I’ve also explained which editors actually deserve a spot on a low-spec Windows PC, and one honest weakness for each, because none of them got everything right.

My scoring method when choosing lightweight PDF editors for Windows

The trigger for this test was a 2018 ThinkPad with 8GB of RAM. If a lightweight PDF editor for Windows can’t hold up there, it’s not lightweight, but just marketed that way. That threshold isn’t arbitrary: Microsoft’s own published minimum for Windows 11 is 4GB of RAM, so an 8GB machine already has less headroom for a PDF app than most users assume. I tested every tool after a fresh restart. Here’s what I actually measured:

  • Install size: The footprint on disk right after setup, portable builds included.
  • RAM usage: Idle after launch, then again after 10 minutes of real editing (typing text, adding an image, running OCR on a page).
  • Launch time: Cold start, from double-click to a usable, responsive window.
  • File open time for large/scanned PDFs: How long each tool took to open my 400-page scanned manual and my 40MB report, since this is where “lightweight” apps most often choke.
  • Background processes: Whether anything kept running or auto-launching after I closed the app, since a few PDF tools install helper services you don’t ask for.

I didn’t chase CPU-cycle precision here. Task Manager readings drift a few percent run to run. But I ran each test three times and used the middle result, and the gaps between tools were consistently large enough to trust.

Editor vs. Reader: Why this distinction matters

Most “best free lightweight PDF editor” lists are really reviewing PDF readers, and that distinction matters if you need to edit a file. Readers feel fast because they only render pages, and don’t handle text editing, image replacement, or form logic.

While editors have to parse the PDF structure, preserve layout, and save those changes cleanly. That’s why every tool below uses a bit more RAM than a viewer. They’re all genuine editors, not just fast page turners.

Quick comparison: All four tools side by side

The table below pulls the score-line numbers from each section into one view, so you can compare install footprint, RAM, and speed without scrolling through four separate write-ups.

PDNob: The Premium Editor That’s Lighter Than I Expected

Score line:

  • Install size ~561MB.
  • RAM (idle/editing) ~89.6MB / ~570MB.
  • Launch time ~2.8s.
  • Large/scanned file open ~4.3s.

PDNob surprised me. For a tool that bundles OCR, AI summarization, and full text/image editing, I expected Acrobat-level bloat, but it stayed responsive throughout my testing. Editing text, replacing images, and reorganizing pages never froze, and the OCR accuracy on my scanned manual matched its strong reputation.

Where it struggles:

The free version also limits AI features, adds watermarks after 20 exports, caps OCR and file conversions to once a week, and restricts batch processing to five files.  But, compared to other PDF editors with similar features, PDNob offers a one-time purchase option that is very affordable.

Best for: It’s the lightest PDF editor for users who want Acrobat-level editing features without Acrobat’s install size or subscription price.

Xournal++: The minimalist free and Open-source option

Score line: 

  • Install size ~95MB.
  • RAM (idle/editing) ~60MB / ~110MB.
  • Launch time ~1.1s.
  • Large/scanned file open ~4.9s.

Xournal++ was the lightest tool I tested by a wide margin, and it’s the first one I’d recommend to anyone looking for an open-source lightweight PDF editor. It launched almost instantly, used very little RAM, and stayed perfectly smooth while I annotated a dense, image-heavy PDF. That lines up with long-time user feedback, which consistently describes it as lightweight, fast on older hardware, and privacy-focused.

Where it struggles:

This isn’t a true PDF content editor. You can’t rewrite text, replace images, or edit form fields. It’s built for annotation, not document editing, and I also noticed occasional CPU and battery spikes during longer freehand drawing sessions despite its tiny RAM footprint.

Best for: Students and researchers who mark up PDFs, like highlighting, sketching, and handwritten notes, rather than rewriting their content.

PDF-XChange Editor Portable: The No-Install, Take-It-Anywhere Option

Score line: 

  • Install size 0MB (runs from USB, ~430MB unpacked).
  • RAM (idle/editing) ~150MB / ~280MB.
  • Launch time ~3.1s.
  • Large/scanned file open ~3.7s.

This is the official portable lightweight PDF editor, so there’s nothing to install. Just unzip it to a USB drive and run. It’s lightweight in system footprint rather than RAM, making it ideal for locked-down PCs or anyone who doesn’t want another installed app. Despite being portable, it opens large files quickly and includes genuine text, object editing, annotation, and OCR instead of the stripped-down feature set most portable PDF apps offer.

Where it struggles: 

The free version adds watermarks when you use paid features, and it can load a bit slower than some rivals. That’s a fair trade-off, though, considering how much editing functionality is packed into a single portable executable.

Best for: People who work across multiple or shared Windows machines and want real editing power without leaving an install behind.

Stirling-PDF: The Browser-Based, Privacy-First Option

Score line:

  • Install size N/A (Docker container, image ~600MB).
  • RAM ~250MB baseline server load.
  • Launch time instant once running (browser tab).
  • Large/scanned file open ~5 8s depending on server hardware.

Stirling-PDF isn’t a Windows app at all. It’s a self-hosted Docker container you access through a browser, so “install size” is a different question. In return, you get the strongest privacy on this list. It’s a free, open-source tool with 60+ PDF operations that keeps every file on your own hardware. If keeping documents off third-party servers matters to you, Stirling-PDF is the most complete free option I tested.

Where it struggles:

Self-hosting isn’t a zero-effort setup. You need Docker, a running container, and proper authentication if you’re exposing it beyond your own machine. It’s light in the browser, but the setup happens at the server level, which is a real barrier if you’re not comfortable with the command line.

Best for: Privacy-conscious users, freelancers handling client contracts, or small teams who are already comfortable running a Docker container and want zero third-party file exposure.

How to choose between these Four Lightweight PDF Editors

Match the tool to whichever resource is actually limiting your machine, not to a generic “best PDF editor” ranking. The four tools above solve different constraints, and picking the wrong one means paying for features you’ll never touch or hitting a wall the first time you need real editing.

If RAM is the bottleneck, for example an older laptop with 8GB or less, Xournal++’s 60MB idle footprint gives the most headroom, but only if annotation covers your needs. If you need actual text and image editing on that same low-RAM machine, PDF-XChange Editor Portable is the better fit since its RAM usage stays under 300MB even while editing.

If you switch between computers, a shared office PC, a library machine, a friend’s laptop, the portable option removes the “can I even install software here” question entirely. And if your PDFs contain anything sensitive, contracts, medical records, financial statements, Stirling-PDF’s self-hosted model is the only one on this list where files never leave hardware you control.

PDNob sits in the middle: it’s the only tool here with AI summarization and batch OCR, so it’s worth the extra install size if you process PDFs often enough that those features save real time.

Final Verdict

There’s no single “lightweight PDF editor.” It depends on what’s limiting your machine. Xournal++ is the clear winner for RAM and CPU if annotation is enough. PDF-XChange Editor Portable is the best all-round portable editor, and PDNob offers the strongest editing features without the bloat. While Stirling-PDF is the top choice if privacy is non-negotiable. Match the tool to your real constraint, and any of these four beats defaulting to Acrobat out of habit.

FAQs

Is there a lightweight alternative to Adobe Acrobat for Windows?

Yes. All four tools tested here are built as smaller, faster alternatives to Acrobat. PDNob comes closest to matching Acrobat’s editing depth while staying under 600MB installed, and PDF-XChange Editor covers most of Acrobat’s day-to-day functions in a portable build with no installer at all.

Is a portable PDF editor safer or more private than an installed one?

No, Photographic Styles are designed for still photos and do not affect video recordings.

Portability and privacy are separate things. A portable app like PDF-XChange Editor Portable avoids leaving an installation footprint on a shared PC, but it still processes files locally the same way an installed editor does. For actual data privacy, a self-hosted option like Stirling-PDF is the stronger choice since files never leave your own server.

Is there an open-source lightweight PDF editor?

Yes. Xournal++ and Stirling-PDF are both open-source in this test. Xournal++ is a lightweight desktop app built for annotation, while Stirling-PDF is a self-hosted, browser-based tool with 60+ PDF operations that keeps every file on your own hardware.

mainEntity.name: Is there a lightweight alternative to Adobe Acrobat for Windows?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. All four tools tested here are built as smaller, faster alternatives to Acrobat. PDNob comes closest to matching Acrobat's editing depth while staying under 600MB installed, and PDF-XChange Editor covers most of Acrobat's day-to-day functions in a portable build with no installer at all.

mainEntity.name: Is a portable PDF editor safer or more private than an installed one?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Photographic Styles are designed for still photos and do not affect video recordings. Portability and privacy are separate things. A portable app like PDF-XChange Editor Portable avoids leaving an installation footprint on a shared PC, but it still processes files locally the same way an installed editor does. For actual data privacy, a self-hosted option like Stirling-PDF is the stronger choice since files never leave your own server.

mainEntity.name: Is there an open-source lightweight PDF editor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Xournal++ and Stirling-PDF are both open-source in this test. Xournal++ is a lightweight desktop app built for annotation, while Stirling-PDF is a self-hosted, browser-based tool with 60+ PDF operations that keeps every file on your own hardware.

title.rendered: Fortnite teases Simpsons crossover: Here’s what we know

content.rendered:
After months of rumors, The Simpsons finally looks set to return to Fortnite, as teased by the game’s official social media account. On July 23, a video about this highly awaited collaboration was shared, enthusing fans of the animated sitcom.

Although similarly popular franchises debuted in Fortnite years ago, The Simpsons first landed in the online title rather recently, in late 2025. The highlight of that collab was the Springfield map, which replaced the default one for a month in Battle Royale. It also packed various relevant skins inspired by pivotal characters like Homer Simpson, along with other themed cosmetics and in-game events.

Fortnite x Simpsons teaser breakdown

The six-second clip of the Fortnite x Simpsons collab provides a bird’s-eye-view glimpse at the returning Springfield map, first introduced in November 2025 during Chapter 6. Unlike the last time, Springfield Island seems to be coming to Fortnite Reload instead of Battle Royale, as indicated by the text at the beginning of the teaser. The post also mentions Bart, Lisa, and Krusty the Clown, who will probably be added as skins. Importantly, everything that’s part of the latest collab has been confirmed to be unveiled on July 29.

I miss my friends: Bart, Lisa, Krusty…

Full reveal on July 29. pic.twitter.com/ja4irjY32G

— Fortnite (@Fortnite) July 23, 2026

Notably, the opening moments show a Slurp Co. blimp-powered Battle Bus, a fictional beverage company specifically developed for Fortnite’s collab with The Simpsons last year. It is responsible for manufacturing Slurp, a Fortnite audience-friendly replacement for the long-running sitcom’s alcoholic beverage named Duff Beer.

In the comments, several fans expressed excitement over the return of Springfield and fan-favorite character, Krusty the Clown, in Fortnite. While some fans requested new Simpsons-themed items for the forthcoming content drop, others shared their interest in a new Fortnite mini-season based on the animated show.

Wrapping up

Fortnite’s original Simpsons collab was a long-overdue coming together of two huge pop culture entities, and it was quite successful as well. Hence, it’s not surprising that players are buzzing again at the news of Springfield making a comeback to the multiplayer game.

According to reputed leakers, such as Shiina and FireMonkey, the collab is expected to land in the update coming this week, on July 30. This date has been known since the leaks, extracted from Fortnite’s survey, surfaced two weeks ago around July 16. In other words, the anticipation around Fortnite x Simpsons that has been building up over the past several days is soon going to reach its culmination, thanks to the next content refresh rolling out very soon.

FAQs

How many times has Simpsons collaborated with Fortnite before?

So far, only one Fortnite x Simpsons collab has been released. It came out in November 2025.

Which was the most popular thing about the previous Fortnite x Simpsons collab?

The Springfield Island map was arguably the most well-received addition and hence the most popular thing to emerge out of the collab.

Which other animated sitcoms have partnered with Fortnite in the past?

Plenty of different shows from that category, including South Park, Family Guy, and Rick & Morty, have previously collaborated with Fortnite.

mainEntity.name: Is there a lightweight alternative to Adobe Acrobat for Windows?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. All four tools tested here are built as smaller, faster alternatives to Acrobat. PDNob comes closest to matching Acrobat's editing depth while staying under 600MB installed, and PDF-XChange Editor covers most of Acrobat's day-to-day functions in a portable build with no installer at all.

mainEntity.name: Is a portable PDF editor safer or more private than an installed one?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Photographic Styles are designed for still photos and do not affect video recordings. Portability and privacy are separate things. A portable app like PDF-XChange Editor Portable avoids leaving an installation footprint on a shared PC, but it still processes files locally the same way an installed editor does. For actual data privacy, a self-hosted option like Stirling-PDF is the stronger choice since files never leave your own server.

mainEntity.name: Is there an open-source lightweight PDF editor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Xournal++ and Stirling-PDF are both open-source in this test. Xournal++ is a lightweight desktop app built for annotation, while Stirling-PDF is a self-hosted, browser-based tool with 60+ PDF operations that keeps every file on your own hardware.

title.rendered: Grand Piece Online – GPO codes (November 2026)

content.rendered:
Update: Verified the latest Grand Piece Online Codes on November 12, 2026

Grand Piece Online codes can save you hours of grinding by handing out double EXP, better drop rates, race rerolls, stat resets, and Tailor Vouchers. These freebies make leveling up, farming rare items, and experimenting with different builds much easier, especially if you’re just starting out or returning after an update.

The catch is that GPO codes disappear unusually fast, so old lists become useless within days. That’s why it’s worth redeeming every active code as soon as possible before it expires.

All working Grand Piece Online codes

  • ILOVEGPO_7: 3 Tailor Vouchers (NEW)
  • HAPPYHALLOWEEN_Drops11: 48 Hours of 2x Drops (NEW)
  • FREE_EXP10: 1 Day of 2x Drop Rates (NEW)
  • ILOVEGPO_6 NEW: 3 Tailor Vouchers
  • HAPPYHALLOWEEN_Drops10: 48 Hours of 2x Drops
  • FREE_Drops8: 1 Day of 2x Drop Rates
  • ILOVEGPO_3: 2x Tailor Vouchers
  • FREE_Drops7: 1 Day of 2x Drop Rates
  • FREE_EXP6: 3 Days of 2x Exp

Expired Grand Piece Online codes

10FREERACEREROLLS!!!, 1BILLIONVISTS10RACEREROLLS, 1BILLIONVISTS2XDROP, 1BILLIONVISTS2XEXP, 1BILLIONVISTS2XEXP4, 1MILLIONLIKES2XDROP, 1MILLIONLIKES2XEXP, 1MILLIONLIKESRACEREROLLS, 1MILLIONLIKESSPRESET, 3FREETAILORVOUCHERS!, 5FREETAILORVOUCHERS_2, 5FREETAILORVOUCHERS_3, 900K30REROLLS, ANIGRIND1, ANIGRIND3, ANOTHER3FREETAILORVOUCHERS!, BENERE, CUPIDGRIND2, CUPIDQUEENDROPS, CUPIDQUEENDROPS2, CUPIDQUEENEXP, CUPIDQUEENEXP2, DMHNDKLGFJDFG, FDSGIDSGUS, FREE10ROLLS5, FREE2XDROP!!, FREE2XDROP112025, FREE2XEXP!!!!, FREESPRESET1, FREESPRESET2, FREESPRESET3, FREE_DROPS3, FREE_DROPS6, FREE_EXP3, HALLOWEEN20252SPRESET, HALLOWEEN20252XDROPCODE, HALLOWEEN20252XEXP, HALLOWEEN2025RACEREROLLCODE, HALLOWEENPART22XEXP, HALLOWEENPART32XEXP, HAPPYNEWYEARS!, HAPPYNEWYEARS!2, HAPPYNEWYEARS2026_1, HAPPYNEWYEARS2026_2, HEADLESSRACEREROLLS, ILOVEGPO_2, LOTSOFREROLLS, LOTSOFREROLLS10, LUCKYDROPS, LUCKYDROPS10, LUCKYDROPS11, LUCKYDROPS13, LUCKYDROPS2, LUCKYDROPS3, LUCKYDROPS4, LUCKYDROPS6, LUCKYDROPS7, LUCKYDROPS8, LUCKYREROLLS, LUCKYREROLLS2, LUCKYREROLLS5LUCKYREROLLS4, MERRYCHRISTMAS1, MERRYCHRISTMAS2, MERRYCHRISTMAS2025_1, MERRYCHRISTMAS2025_2, MERRYCHRISTMASEVE1, MOBILEISOUT, MOBILEISOUT3, MOBILEISOUT4, MOBILEISOUT5, MOBILESOON, MOBILESOON2, MOBILESOON3, MOBILESOON4, PHOGIVING20252XDROPS, PHOGIVING20252XEXP, PRESTIGEWORLDENDERGRIND!!, PRESTIGEWORLDENDERGRIND2!!, REAL10FREERACEREROLLS, RUMBLINGDELAY_1, RUMBLINGDELAY_2, RUMBLINGDELAY_3, SDFSFSD, VALENTINESSOON_1, VALENTINESSOON_2, XLOTSOFREROLLS4, XLOTSOFREROLLS5

How to redeem Grand Piece Online codes

The code box may appear under Settings or Shop, depending on the current game layout and your device.

  1. Open Grand Piece Online on Roblox.
  2. Select Set Sail and load into the game.
  3. Press M or tap the Menu button.
  4. Open the Shop.
  5. Paste a code into the redemption box.
  6. Press Enter to claim the reward.

GPO codes are case-sensitive. Copy the whole string, but remove any accidental space at the end before pressing Enter.

Why your GPO code may not work

Most failed redemptions come down to one of these issues:

  • The code expired: GPO codes often last only 24 to 48 hours.
  • The text is wrong: Capital letters, underscores, and exclamation marks must match.
  • A space was pasted: Delete any blank space before or after the code.
  • You already used it: Each code normally works once per Roblox account.
  • Your server is old: Leave the game, join a fresh server, and try once more.

If a correctly copied code still fails in a new server, move on. Re-entering it repeatedly will not revive an expired reward.

mainEntity.name: Is there a lightweight alternative to Adobe Acrobat for Windows?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. All four tools tested here are built as smaller, faster alternatives to Acrobat. PDNob comes closest to matching Acrobat's editing depth while staying under 600MB installed, and PDF-XChange Editor covers most of Acrobat's day-to-day functions in a portable build with no installer at all.

mainEntity.name: Is a portable PDF editor safer or more private than an installed one?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Photographic Styles are designed for still photos and do not affect video recordings. Portability and privacy are separate things. A portable app like PDF-XChange Editor Portable avoids leaving an installation footprint on a shared PC, but it still processes files locally the same way an installed editor does. For actual data privacy, a self-hosted option like Stirling-PDF is the stronger choice since files never leave your own server.

mainEntity.name: Is there an open-source lightweight PDF editor?
