title.rendered: Apple reportedly negotiating lower OLED panel costs ahead of iPhone 18 launch

content.rendered:
Apple is reportedly negotiating lower OLED panel prices with Samsung Display and LG Display for the upcoming iPhone 18 Pro Max as it looks to offset rising memory and storage costs.

According to The Elec, Apple is aiming to pay around $70 per OLED panel, although industry sources expect the final negotiated price to settle at approximately $66.50 per panel. If the negotiations are successful, Apple could secure one of its largest OLED panel cost reductions in recent years.

Apple has historically negotiated lower display prices with each new iPhone generation, but this year’s talks appear more aggressive. The company is reportedly seeking a deeper price cut even as Samsung Display and LG Display prepare to manufacture the new M16 OLED panels for the iPhone 18 Pro lineup.

Apple wants lower prices for a more advanced display

The iPhone 18 Pro models are expected to feature Samsung Display’s new M16 OLED material set, which is designed to deliver improved brightness efficiency, better color accuracy, and a longer display lifespan.

However, the upgraded display technology is also more difficult and expensive to manufacture. Suppliers will need to improve production yields before they can scale up mass production efficiently.

Earlier reports have also suggested that the iPhone 18 Pro lineup will adopt LTPO+ display technology, adding another significant upgrade to Apple’s flagship displays.

According to the report, Samsung Display is expected to supply around 46 million OLED panels for the iPhone 18 family, while LG Display could manufacture an additional 41 million panels.

Most of those displays are expected to be used in the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, although both suppliers are also reportedly preparing OLED panels for Apple’s first foldable iPhone.

Higher iPhone prices are still possible

Even if Apple succeeds in lowering OLED panel costs, the savings may not be enough to offset the continued rise in memory and storage prices.

Memory and NAND flash costs have continued increasing across the semiconductor industry, adding further pressure to the manufacturing costs of premium smartphones.

Apple is expected to unveil the iPhone 18 Pro lineup this September. While lower OLED panel prices could help reduce production costs, rising component prices elsewhere in the supply chain may still result in higher retail prices for consumers.

Whether Apple absorbs those additional costs or passes them on to buyers remains to be seen.

Do you think Apple will use these display cost savings to keep iPhone prices stable, or is another price increase for the iPhone 18 Pro lineup inevitable? Let us know in the comments below.

mainEntity.name: Is there a lightweight alternative to Adobe Acrobat for Windows?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. All four tools tested here are built as smaller, faster alternatives to Acrobat. PDNob comes closest to matching Acrobat's editing depth while staying under 600MB installed, and PDF-XChange Editor covers most of Acrobat's day-to-day functions in a portable build with no installer at all.

mainEntity.name: Is a portable PDF editor safer or more private than an installed one?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Photographic Styles are designed for still photos and do not affect video recordings. Portability and privacy are separate things. A portable app like PDF-XChange Editor Portable avoids leaving an installation footprint on a shared PC, but it still processes files locally the same way an installed editor does. For actual data privacy, a self-hosted option like Stirling-PDF is the stronger choice since files never leave your own server.

mainEntity.name: Is there an open-source lightweight PDF editor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Xournal++ and Stirling-PDF are both open-source in this test. Xournal++ is a lightweight desktop app built for annotation, while Stirling-PDF is a self-hosted, browser-based tool with 60+ PDF operations that keeps every file on your own hardware.

title.rendered: Every GTA protagonist, ranked from worst to best

content.rendered:
Courtesy of its longevity, GTA has a wide variety of protagonists across its highly successful titles. From an unsophisticated immigrant like Niko Bellic to a through-and-through American gangster like Carl Johnson, the broad spectrum of main characters is quite exceptional. As excitement builds for GTA 6, you can also check out the GTA 6 PC system requirements to see if your gaming rig is ready for Rockstar’s next blockbuster.

For this ranked list, we will keep the character development and the charismatic appeal of these GTA protagonists throughout their respective games in mind for deciding the order. Since there was only very limited focus on story elements in the earliest GTA titles, we will be exclusively considering main characters starting from GTA 3. So, with that clear, let’s jump right into it without further ado.

Best GTA main characters

1. Niko Bellic

Chronicling the escapades of Niko Bellic, an immigrant who reluctantly gets embroiled in Liberty City’s crime landscape, GTA 4 expertly tells how the American Dream can quickly come crashing down in a world where expectations are gravely different from reality. This bleak narrative is one of the biggest reasons why GTA fans often rank the 2008 blockbuster hit as the best entry in the series. Another big reason is the equally dark and impactful background of its protagonist.

Having served in the war at a young age, Niko has seen and even been a participant in some of the cruelest crimes against humanity, something that he expresses remorse for throughout the course of the story. However, his continuation of similar deeds post-war implies he has grown insensitive towards such action and would get involved in the same whenever push comes to shove.

Although a stone-cold killer, Niko is still someone who values connections and looks out for his family. Despite Roman selling him lies about his life in America for years, he forgives him sooner rather than later and starts helping him out with the issues Roman faces with the miscreants in the city. His interactions with other NPCs throughout the game also emphasize his inner kindness that has somehow outlasted the torments of war, adding to what makes his character so appealing and memorable.

Besides the GTA 4 lead’s quest for protecting his cousin brother from trouble, Niko’s time in Liberty City has another purpose, which is to get closure on a haunting past and ultimately leave its ghosts behind. Niko is essentially a broken human, but regardless of that, he strives to fix what’s wrong in the lives of those around him, all while showing a level of empathy and generosity you wouldn’t expect of a hired gun.

2. Carl “CJ” Johnson

There may not be a GTA title as timeless as 2004’s GTA San Andreas. And, besides other factors, a huge credit for that goes to its charismatic protagonist Carl Johnson and Young Maylay’s portrayal of him that has immortalized the character in gaming history.

As the brother of Sweet, the head of the Grove Street Families gang, CJ takes it upon himself to gain the favor of the gang back and revitalize its dwindling influence in Los Santos. That tall order sees CJ constantly face new challenges and overcome them, as he moves across all three major cities, Los Santos, San Fierro, and Las Venturas, while running errands for various clients. In the process, he also antagonizes rival gangs such as the Ballas and draws the ire of corrupt police officers.

Throughout the game’s story, CJ’s devotion and loyalty to his gang stand as an exemplary character trait, making him a likable protagonist. Moreover, the resilience he shows in building the Grove Street Families back from scratch is also worth mentioning. Apart from these endearing attributes, the Los Santos-born hoodlum’s witty lines in the game also make for entertaining moments.

3. Trevor Philips

Just ask anyone who has finished GTA 5 about Trevor, and they will tell you how he’s simultaneously the most hilarious and the most insane main character in the franchise’s history. This high-adrenaline mercenary isn’t just cold-blooded but also a complete oddball in the truest sense possible, with a penchant for attracting trouble rather consistently.

Perhaps the most interesting thing about Trevor is that he is as much of a cruel person as he is an emotional person. This strikes a clear contrast between the two prominent sides of his personality, one that is callous enough to kill someone for petty reasons and the other that is sentimental enough to thoroughly experience the pain of betrayal caused by a close friend.

Regardless, a common thread that runs through all that is the character’s unhinged nature, which notably gives birth to some of the most memorable parts of GTA 5’s campaign.

4. Tommy Vercetti

If you think about it, Tommy Vercetti is arguably the one GTA protagonist who finished off, at the end of the story, much stronger than he started. His arc of falling victim to a drug bust to snatching absolute power over Vice City’s underworld is the classic tale of a gangster’s meteoric rise.

In 2002’s GTA Vice City, Vercetti is portrayed as a highly capable hustler, forming useful alliances to track down his target and taking over a criminal empire in the process. The steady pace at which he expands his empire and grows the businesses he purchases forms a significant part of Vice City’s missions, highlighting that the protagonist isn’t all about brawn but also has the brains needed to keep organized crime thriving.

It’s worth noting that Vercetti is also someone who can tell the importance of keeping trusted allies close and of promptly neutralizing his enemies, whether outside or within his circle. The Vice City protagonist’s adventures set in the ’80s are like a reflection of Tony Montana’s in the popular 1983 film Scarface, but minus the decline.

5. Johnny Klebitz

In GTA 4: The Lost And Damned (2009), Johnny Klebitz is a battle-hardened veteran of The Lost Motorcycle Club. As its vice-president, he is very focused on keeping the organization afloat by finding ways to maintain cash flow and avoid unnecessary conflict with rival gangs in Alderney.

Even though Klebitz is officially only the second man-in-charge when the story begins, his remarkably responsible way of going about his club duties portrays him as a level-headed person compared to other members of The Lost, in particular Club President Billy Grey. Johnny’s sympathy and care for his drug-addicted ex Ashley Butler provide a glimpse of his soft side and paint him as more of a complex figure than just an unruly and intimidating biker.

The rise of Klebitz to the undisputed top of The Lost MC and the eventual fate of the group tells a story of desperate survival, internal conflict, and reconciliation with harsh realities. Amidst an overall dark narrative, the pragmatic personality of the Lost And Damned protagonist shines bright.

6. Michael De Santa

Living the dream life doesn’t equate to living a happy life—at least, that’s the message Michael de Santa’s story embodies in GTA 5. Despite having a lavish home in a posh area of Los Santos and despite having a family complete with a wife and two kids, the protagonist’s need to seek therapy for his domestic issues shows the dark reality about the inefficacy of wealth in certain important aspects of life.

One of the key things about Michael is his ability to survive through the most unpredictable situations and turn the tide in his favor. We see that in the game’s prologue, then in his entanglement with a drug cartel leader, all the way through the canon final mission of Rockstar’s best-selling title.

The middle-aged lead, despite his drawbacks, comes off as a very human character who just wants to have the simple joys in life and is willing to do everything he can to make things conducive to that scenario.

7. Luis Fernando López

Luis Lopez’s climb in life gives off the vibe of a rags-to-riches tale or an overnight success story. But the heights he reaches in his 20s aren’t exactly due to his own efforts but instead more of a consequence of joining allegiance with eminent nightclub owner Gay Tony as his bodyguard. While that one is a positive consequence, the less positive ones are what make up the meat of GTA 4: The Ballad Of Gay Tony’s campaign.

The Dominican-American hustler is the archetypal youth still finding his feet in a career his parents—more specifically, his mother—don’t approve of. Despite that opposition, the love for one’s mother and one’s family isn’t lost on him as, in the 2009 expansion game, he is depicted as being someone who deeply cares for and looks after his own.

Beyond those relations, Lopez’s character shows more integrity by tirelessly helping his long-time friend and benefactor Gay Tony and by not giving up on him in spite of the latter’s worsening financial troubles—proof that loyalty doesn’t always need to emerge out of sharing a creed or clan.

8. Franklin Clinton

Being the youngest of the three protagonists in 2013’s GTA 5, Franklin Clinton is someone who stands out in the trio for being relatively inexperienced in the criminal world. The character’s uniqueness in the action-adventure title also comes down to the fact that he appears to be the most “normal” protagonist compared to Michael and Trevor.

Despite not being a long-time felon like the majority of GTA protagonists, Franklin is still able to pull off demanding assignments, emerging as resourceful and ambitious. Moreover, his temperament, which lets him juggle his professional and personal lives while still maintaining some sort of sanity, is a glaringly praiseworthy attribute.

Safe to say, he acts as the glue keeping the GTA 5 triad together and the voice of reason sandwiched between Trevor’s brash recklessness and Michael’s eternally frustrated attitude.

9. Toni Cipriani

First introduced in GTA 3 as one of Claude’s clients who gives him missions, Toni Cipriani got a full-fledged primary role in GTA Liberty City Stories, which was released in 2005. The Italian-origin hitman’s extreme loyalty towards the Leone Crime Family and his complicated relationship with his mother are two prominent aspects of the character exhibited throughout the game.

Cipriani’s rapid ascent that sees him go from a pawn in Salvatore Leone’s crime family to eventually earning the trust of the kingpin himself is an intriguing insight into his brutal dedication toward the criminal organization.

By the end of Liberty City Stories’s course, the hot-headed protagonist establishes himself as someone who puts the collective’s interest ahead of his own and has it in him to go to any length for fulfilling the same—traits that are well-explored through the entirety of the PSP-era game.

10. Victor Vance

There may not be another GTA character who took as big a leap as Victor Vance did when he went from a forgettable tertiary role in 2002’s Vice City to the all-important protagonist in Vice City Stories that released four years later. While closer to a husk of a character in the former, the latter portrayed Vance as one of the few GTA anti-heroes with a surviving conscience.

The journey Vance takes from unfairly losing his job in the army to unintentionally kickstarting his own crime family is nothing short of an intriguing twist of fate. His story, of someone pushed into a life of crime by harsh circumstances and then rising to the top of the criminal ladder, is one that undoubtedly leaves a lasting impression.

11. Huang Lee

Huang Lee is the typical prodigal son and arguably the best protagonist ever in a top-down view GTA game. From being an aimless scion of the Triad criminal organization to becoming capable enough to avenge his late father, Lee’s character trajectory shown in 2010’s GTA Chinatown Wars is truly something remarkable to watch unfold.

12. Mike

Mike is certainly one of the more well-written protagonists of GTA’s 2D era. Despite relying on just text to channel his character traits, the leading man of 2004’s GTA Advance still has enough of a story going around him to keep players interested. The deeply personal motive for Mike’s actions early in the game, combined with the plot twist that happens later, makes for an amusing experience.

13. Claude

It feels somewhat unfair to compare Claude with other protagonists, as it was Rockstar’s decision, spurred by both artistic choice and limited resources, not to have any lines recorded for the GTA 3 lead. As such, he doesn’t have any memorable quotes or iconic voiceover that fans remember him from.

However, 25 years later, Claude being mute itself is a trait that helps him stand out in the long list of GTA main characters, while also giving him a “cold and calculated” demeanor. His revenge saga in Liberty City is a cliché yet entertaining trope and, at that time, it was responsible for giving players their first taste of a meaningful storyline in a GTA game.

Rounding up

So, with that, we come to the end of our list. Based on the general consensus in the GTA community, I assume it was no surprise to see Niko and CJ leading the rankings. However, what I’m more interested in knowing is which of these two fan-favorites you would pick as the number-one GTA protagonist and why. Tell us your answer or your own personal ranked list of these characters in the comments below!

On the other hand, you may also share how you feel the two protagonists in GTA 6, Jason and Lucia, will compare to those that have come before them. Personally, judging from what I experienced in Rockstar’s latest work, Red Dead Redemption 2, I think they will surely be among the most well-written and complex GTA protagonists we have seen in the franchise yet. If you’re excited for the next game, don’t miss our complete GTA 6 weapon list to see the arsenal Rockstar has revealed so far.

mainEntity.name: Is there a lightweight alternative to Adobe Acrobat for Windows?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. All four tools tested here are built as smaller, faster alternatives to Acrobat. PDNob comes closest to matching Acrobat's editing depth while staying under 600MB installed, and PDF-XChange Editor covers most of Acrobat's day-to-day functions in a portable build with no installer at all.

mainEntity.name: Is a portable PDF editor safer or more private than an installed one?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Photographic Styles are designed for still photos and do not affect video recordings. Portability and privacy are separate things. A portable app like PDF-XChange Editor Portable avoids leaving an installation footprint on a shared PC, but it still processes files locally the same way an installed editor does. For actual data privacy, a self-hosted option like Stirling-PDF is the stronger choice since files never leave your own server.

mainEntity.name: Is there an open-source lightweight PDF editor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Xournal++ and Stirling-PDF are both open-source in this test. Xournal++ is a lightweight desktop app built for annotation, while Stirling-PDF is a self-hosted, browser-based tool with 60+ PDF operations that keeps every file on your own hardware.

title.rendered: Apple sued after fake Sparrow Wallet app allegedly stole $1.8 million

content.rendered:
Three iPhone users have sued Apple after allegedly losing Bitcoin worth about $1.8 million through a fake Sparrow Wallet app on the App Store.

The complaint filed on July 24 argues that Apple’s promises of App Store safety led James Ramirez, Christopher Ellis, and Jalen Delgado to trust the fraudulent app. The plaintiffs say it captured their Bitcoin seed phrases and transferred their funds to wallets controlled by scammers.

The case was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California. Its claims are allegations, and the court has not found Apple liable.

The plaintiffs say they lost $1.835 million

The alleged thefts happened over several months in 2025:

  • Delgado says he lost about $120,000 after downloading a fake Sparrow app on May 1.
  • Ramirez says 7.4 Bitcoin, then worth about $875,000, was taken after he downloaded an app on July 25.
  • Ellis says he lost about $840,000 after finding the app on August 3.

All three say they entered their seed phrases when the app asked for them. Anyone with that recovery phrase can take control of the wallet and move its funds.

Ramirez says he reported the fake app and his loss to Apple on July 25. According to the complaint, Ellis still found it on the App Store nine days later and also reported what happened.

Sparrow Wallet does not have an iPhone app

The real Sparrow Wallet is desktop software. Its official download page lists versions for macOS, Windows, and Linux, but none for iOS or iPadOS.

Sparrow developer Craig Raw had publicly warned about impersonator apps as early as January 2024. The new lawsuit alleges that Apple failed to remove fake listings quickly enough or clearly warn users that App Store review did not confirm a crypto wallet’s identity.

That distinction matters with wallet apps. An App Store listing is not proof that an app belongs to the project it claims to represent. Users should check the developer’s official website before downloading anything and never enter a seed phrase into an unfamiliar app.

The lawsuit targets Apple’s safety claims

The plaintiffs accuse Apple of misleading customers by calling the App Store a safe and trusted place while allegedly failing to stop or respond to reported crypto scams.

They are seeking reimbursement for the stolen funds, compensatory and punitive damages, and court orders that would require stronger review, monitoring, and warnings for cryptocurrency apps.

Apple has faced a similar lawsuit over the Swiftcrypt scam app, which allegedly cost another user more than $80,000. The new case is separate, but both complaints focus on the gap between Apple’s safety marketing and fraudulent apps that reached users.

Apple says its review system combines human checks with automated tools. In its latest App Store fraud report, the company said it rejected more than 2 million problematic app submissions and stopped over $2.2 billion in potentially fraudulent transactions during 2025.

Those figures do not answer the plaintiffs’ specific claims. The case will turn on whether they can show that Apple’s marketing and its alleged handling of reported fake apps made the company legally responsible for their losses.

If you spot an app impersonating a known service, you can report the scam from the App Store or Apple’s Report a Problem page.

mainEntity.name: Is there a lightweight alternative to Adobe Acrobat for Windows?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. All four tools tested here are built as smaller, faster alternatives to Acrobat. PDNob comes closest to matching Acrobat's editing depth while staying under 600MB installed, and PDF-XChange Editor covers most of Acrobat's day-to-day functions in a portable build with no installer at all.

mainEntity.name: Is a portable PDF editor safer or more private than an installed one?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Photographic Styles are designed for still photos and do not affect video recordings. Portability and privacy are separate things. A portable app like PDF-XChange Editor Portable avoids leaving an installation footprint on a shared PC, but it still processes files locally the same way an installed editor does. For actual data privacy, a self-hosted option like Stirling-PDF is the stronger choice since files never leave your own server.

mainEntity.name: Is there an open-source lightweight PDF editor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Xournal++ and Stirling-PDF are both open-source in this test. Xournal++ is a lightweight desktop app built for annotation, while Stirling-PDF is a self-hosted, browser-based tool with 60+ PDF operations that keeps every file on your own hardware.

title.rendered: Cursor vs. GitHub Copilot: Which one should you actually use?

content.rendered:
AI coding tools used to split neatly into two camps: full editors like Cursor, and plugins like GitHub Copilot that bolted onto whatever IDE you already used. That distinction made the choice fairly simple. Do you want a new editor built around AI, or do you want to keep your current setup and add AI on top?

That line has mostly disappeared. GitHub now ships a standalone Copilot desktop app for running multiple coding agents at once, and Cursor has answered with its own Agents Window for the same job. So the real question today isn’t “editor versus plugin.” It’s how each product wants you to organize your work, and which style actually matches how you code.

Here’s the short answer, followed by everything that goes into it. Choose Cursor if you want one AI-native editor where manual coding, chat, and multiple parallel agents all live together. Choose GitHub Copilot if you want your agent work tied directly to GitHub’s issues, PRs, and CI, or if you’d rather keep the editor you already use.

How the two products are actually organized

Cursor is a fork of VS Code with AI built into every layer: completions, chat, an Agent mode, and now an Agents Window for running several agents side by side. Copilot takes a different approach. It lives as a plugin across a dozen editors, adds a separate app for parallel agent work, and also shows up in the command line and on GitHub itself.

If you spend most of your day writing code yourself, Cursor still fits better

Cursor makes sense when your work is mostly reading and editing code, with AI as a constant assistant rather than the main event. Tab predictions, chat, Agent-driven changes, diffs, and a terminal all share one interface, so the loop stays tight. You can accept a suggested change, rewrite the next line yourself, ask Agent to chase down a failing test, and check the result, all without switching tools.

Coming from VS Code makes the move nearly frictionless. Cursor can import your extensions, themes, settings, and keybindings in one pass. It’s still a separate editor day to day, though, and Cursor itself notes that its VS Code base can lag a release or two behind upstream for stability.

Both tools now let you run several agents at once, but they get there differently

Parallel agent work used to be Copilot’s clearest edge. That’s no longer true. Cursor’s Agents Window collects every active agent session, local or cloud, across all your repos, into a single panel. Agents can run in isolated git worktrees, so several tasks can run at the same time without stepping on each other’s changes.

Copilot’s standalone app works the same way in practice: multiple sessions, each with its own worktree and branch, running locally or in GitHub-hosted cloud sandboxes (currently in public preview). Each session can operate in Interactive, Plan, or Autopilot mode, so you can let an agent write code and run tests while you review other work in parallel.

The real difference now is what happens after the code is written. Copilot’s app can pull in context from an existing GitHub issue, open and review pull requests, surface CI results, and merge the change, all without leaving the app. Cursor’s parallel agents are built for shipping code fast inside the editor, but the GitHub side of the job- issues, reviews, and merging- still happens outside it. If your workflow already revolves around GitHub, Copilot removes more of that handoff.

Both also still work inside a regular IDE when you don’t need multiple agents. Copilot’s completions, chat, multi-file edits, and agent mode are available across VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains IDEs, Xcode, Eclipse, and Neovim. Feature support isn’t identical everywhere, so check GitHub’s compatibility matrix if you need one specific capability in your editor.

What each plan actually costs you

Cursor’s free tier is enough to try Tab and Agent for light use. Pro starts at $20 a month and adds extended agent use, frontier models, and cloud agents, with Pro+ and Ultra scaling further for heavier users. Copilot’s free tier includes 2,000 completions a month plus limited agent and CLI access, and Pro jumps to just $10 a month for unlimited completions, cloud agent access, and code review.

If your needs are mostly autocomplete with occasional agent use, Copilot Pro is the better deal outright. But don’t treat either subscription as unlimited AI labor. Cursor meters model usage, and Copilot spends “AI Credits” across chat, agents, reviews, and CLI work. Push either tool hard enough with daily multi-file agent tasks, and you’ll eventually hit an upgrade prompt or a metered overage.

Don’t skip the review step, no matter which one you pick

The model behind either tool matters less than you’d think, since lineups shift too often to plan a subscription around one specific model. What actually matters is context: Cursor keeps your prompts, files, edits, and terminal in one place, while Copilot connects repositories, branches, issues, PRs, and CI to every session.

Whichever you choose, don’t let it merge code unreviewed. Run the tests, read the diff, and watch for invented APIs, missed edge cases, and edits that wandered outside the original request. Running several agents at once makes this more important, not less: more parallel output means more diffs to actually check before anything ships.

Check your privacy settings before you start

Both tools send your prompts and code context to the cloud, so if you’re working with private or regulated code, use your organization’s approved plan and confirm the policy first. Cursor’s Privacy Mode blocks your code from being used in training. Copilot lets individual subscribers opt out of the same thing, and Business plans add centralized controls on top.

The bottom line

Pick Cursor if you:

  • Want manual editing, Tab, chat, and parallel agents living in a single interface
  • Already use VS Code and don’t mind moving to a close cousin
  • Want to keep agent work inside the editor rather than routed through GitHub

Pick GitHub Copilot if you:

  • Want agent sessions tied directly to issues, PRs, CI results, and merging
  • Need to run agents across projects without leaving your GitHub workflow
  • Want to keep your current editor, or just want the cheaper entry point

Cursor is still the sharper editor, and it’s caught up on parallel agent work with the Agents Window. Copilot’s edge is no longer “it can run agents in parallel.” It’s that those agents plug straight into GitHub’s issue tracker, PRs, and CI. For solo, hands-on coding, Cursor remains the pick. For work that needs to move cleanly from issue to merge, Copilot is still the stronger choice, and its $10 Pro tier makes it the better value for most developers.

If neither fits, there’s a third path worth knowing about: a remote coding agent like Codex, which can be monitored and steered from the ChatGPT mobile app while it runs on a connected machine.

mainEntity.name: Is there a lightweight alternative to Adobe Acrobat for Windows?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. All four tools tested here are built as smaller, faster alternatives to Acrobat. PDNob comes closest to matching Acrobat's editing depth while staying under 600MB installed, and PDF-XChange Editor covers most of Acrobat's day-to-day functions in a portable build with no installer at all.

mainEntity.name: Is a portable PDF editor safer or more private than an installed one?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Photographic Styles are designed for still photos and do not affect video recordings. Portability and privacy are separate things. A portable app like PDF-XChange Editor Portable avoids leaving an installation footprint on a shared PC, but it still processes files locally the same way an installed editor does. For actual data privacy, a self-hosted option like Stirling-PDF is the stronger choice since files never leave your own server.

mainEntity.name: Is there an open-source lightweight PDF editor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Xournal++ and Stirling-PDF are both open-source in this test. Xournal++ is a lightweight desktop app built for annotation, while Stirling-PDF is a self-hosted, browser-based tool with 60+ PDF operations that keeps every file on your own hardware.

title.rendered: Apple reportedly planning WWDC 2027 debut for privacy-focused smart glasses

content.rendered:
Apple is reportedly making privacy one of the biggest selling points of its first pair of smart glasses, a strategy that could help the company stand out in a market currently led by products such as the Meta Ray-Ban smart glasses.

According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple is developing new privacy-focused hardware and software features for the wearable and is currently targeting a WWDC 2027 unveiling.

Although Gurman did not reveal the specific privacy features Apple is working on, he said the company plans to make privacy a central part of its marketing strategy. That approach could help Apple differentiate its smart glasses from competing products, many of which have faced criticism over their ability to capture photos and videos without people realizing they are being recorded.

Apple has reportedly tested multiple camera designs

Privacy concerns have reportedly shaped more than just Apple’s software plans.

According to Gurman, Apple has experimented with several hardware designs while developing its smart glasses.

One prototype reportedly featured cameras that supported AI-powered visual features but did not allow users to take photos or record videos. Apple has also tested another version that completely removed the camera system.

Both concepts appear to be aimed at addressing the privacy concerns that have surrounded camera-equipped smart glasses for years.

Despite those experiments, Gurman says Apple’s current plan is still to ship the glasses with built-in cameras. Rather than removing cameras altogether, the company is reportedly exploring hardware and software solutions that make them less intrusive and give users and bystanders greater confidence about when and how the cameras are being used.

A WWDC 2027 launch is currently planned

Beyond their privacy-focused design, Apple’s smart glasses are expected to include speakers and microphones for listening to music, making phone calls, receiving notifications, and interacting with Siri.

In terms of functionality, the device is expected to compete directly with products such as the Meta Ray-Ban smart glasses while placing a stronger emphasis on user privacy.

According to Gurman, Apple is currently targeting a WWDC 2027 announcement, with customer shipments expected to begin later that year.

As with any product still under development, Apple’s plans could change before launch, and both the timeline and final feature set remain subject to change.

If the report proves accurate, Apple’s first smart glasses could represent one of the company’s biggest new product launches since the Vision Pro, with privacy positioned as a key differentiator in an increasingly competitive wearable market.

Would you buy Apple’s smart glasses if they offered stronger privacy protections than Meta’s Ray-Ban smart glasses? Let us know in the comments below.

mainEntity.name: Is there a lightweight alternative to Adobe Acrobat for Windows?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. All four tools tested here are built as smaller, faster alternatives to Acrobat. PDNob comes closest to matching Acrobat's editing depth while staying under 600MB installed, and PDF-XChange Editor covers most of Acrobat's day-to-day functions in a portable build with no installer at all.

mainEntity.name: Is a portable PDF editor safer or more private than an installed one?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Photographic Styles are designed for still photos and do not affect video recordings. Portability and privacy are separate things. A portable app like PDF-XChange Editor Portable avoids leaving an installation footprint on a shared PC, but it still processes files locally the same way an installed editor does. For actual data privacy, a self-hosted option like Stirling-PDF is the stronger choice since files never leave your own server.

mainEntity.name: Is there an open-source lightweight PDF editor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Xournal++ and Stirling-PDF are both open-source in this test. Xournal++ is a lightweight desktop app built for annotation, while Stirling-PDF is a self-hosted, browser-based tool with 60+ PDF operations that keeps every file on your own hardware.

title.rendered: Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 vs Pixel 10 Pro Fold: Here’s the foldable I’d actually buy

content.rendered:
Foldable phones have finally reached the point where choosing one isn’t just about getting a bendable screen. You can choose based on your preference, whether it is productivity, AI, camera or usability.

With the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 now officially announced, Samsung is taking a different approach than previous generations. Instead of simply making the Fold more powerful, it has made it lighter, thinner, and more comfortable to use. Meanwhile, Google’s Pixel 10 Pro Fold continues to focus on photography, AI, and the clean Pixel software experience.

If you’re spending flagship money, here’s which is better: Galaxy Z Fold8 or Pixel 10 Pro Fold in 2026.

Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 vs Google Pixel 10 Pro Fold: Quick specs comparison

Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 vs Google Pixel 10 Pro Fold: Which is better?

Samsung and Google have taken two very different approaches to their latest foldables. The Galaxy Z Fold8 focuses on portability, multitasking, and productivity with a lighter design and a Snapdragon flagship processor. Meanwhile, the Pixel 10 Pro Fold doubles down on AI, computational photography, long-term software support, and a larger foldable display.

None can be considered the overall winner, as each smartphone wins in its own category. Here I have compared Samsung foldable vs Google foldable based on key aspects.

Display comparison

Both foldables feature premium OLED displays with adaptive 120Hz refresh rates and peak brightness of up to 3,000 nits, making them easy to use indoors and outdoors. However, their display philosophies differ.

The Galaxy Z Fold8 features a 7.6-inch 1848 x 2448 Dynamic AMOLED 2X main display and a 5.5-inch 1972 x 1248 cover display. Samsung redesigned the phone with a 4:3 inner aspect ratio and a 10:16 cover screen. I can see myself using it more for multitasking, document editing, spreadsheets, split-screen apps, etc. Moreover, the Vision Booster anti-reflective coating improves outdoor visibility.

Google opts for an even larger 8-inch Super Actua Flex inner display paired with a 6.4-inch outer display. The larger display is useful for reading, watching movies and playing games, while the traditional 20:9 cover display feels familiar when using the phone closed. Both displays support HDR support and smooth 120Hz refresh rates.

Winner: Tie. Choose Galaxy Z Fold8 for productivity and multitasking, and Pixel 10 Pro Fold if you prefer a larger display for entertainment and reading.

Design and build quality: Samsung is lighter, Google is more durable

Samsung made one of the biggest design changes in the Fold series this year. At just 201g and 4.5mm when unfolded, the Galaxy Z Fold8 is significantly lighter than many competing foldables. It’s available in four beautiful colors: Lavender, Cream, Graphite, and Pistachio (Samsung.com exclusive).

I also appreciate Samsung’s new Armor FlexHinge, Armor Aluminum frame, Gorilla Glass protection, and dual-layer Flex Titanium reinforcement beneath the display for added durability. However, it’s only IP48 rated. So, I would be cautious about water damage.

Google takes a durability-first approach. The Pixel 10 Pro Fold weighs 258g but offers IP68 dust and water resistance, Gorilla Glass Victus 2, and a reinforced aerospace-grade aluminum hinge. I really like the hand feel of its silky matte back with a satin-finish aluminum frame. But there are only two colors: Moonstone and Jade.

Furthermore, Google explains that all major elements are made out of recycled materials. Overall, the full dust and fingerprint resistance remains rare among foldables, giving Pixel a notable advantage for long-term durability.

Winner: Galaxy Z Fold8 for portability and premium feel. Pixel 10 Pro Fold for durability and better environmental protection.

Performance: Snapdragon Power vs Tensor Intelligence

Performance is where Samsung gains an edge.

The Galaxy Z Fold8 is powered by the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5, Qualcomm’s latest flagship processor optimized specifically for Samsung devices. Combined with up to 16GB RAM and next-gen CPU, GPU, and NPU gains, I am sure it delivers more gaming headroom, better sustained performance of demanding workloads, improved AI capabilities, and faster multitasking.

Google equips the Pixel 10 Pro Fold with the Tensor G5 processor and standard 16GB RAM. While Tensor chips are not designed to top benchmark charts, they provide an extra boost to Google’s AI features, image processing, speech recognition, and on-device machine learning. Based on my experience, day-to-day performance is fluid, although some heavy games may occasionally struggle.

Winner: Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 for more raw performance.

Camera comparison: Google brings the bigger photography flex

Google continues to prioritize computational photography.

The Pixel 10 Pro Fold features a 48MP Quad PD wide main camera, 10.5MP dual PD ultrawide with Macro focus, and 10.8MP 5x telephoto camera with OIS and Super Res Zoom up to 20x. Google’s software features, including Camera Coach, Magic Eraser, Best Take, Photo Unblur, Reimagine, hands-free astrophotography, and much more, consistently produce some of the best smartphone photos available.

Samsung takes a creator-focused approach with dual 50MP rear cameras, 8K video recording support, Nightography, ProVisual Engine, and Dual Recording. You will also get 2x optical-quality zoom and a 100-degree field of view. I liked how the Fold8 makes excellent use of its folding design to preview shots, record with multiple cameras simultaneously, and edit content comfortably on the large display.

When it comes to photography, Google’s computational photography is the winner. If you’re a content creator and record videos, edit social media content, or use the foldable screen while shooting, Samsung is more suitable for you.

Winner: Pixel 10 Pro Fold

Battery life and charging: Close on paper, different in practice

Battery capacity alone doesn’t tell the whole story.

Samsung includes a 4,800mAh battery rated for up to 26 hours of video playback. You get up to 63% charge in around 30 min of wired charging with a 45W adapter and a 3A USB-C cable. It also supports 20W fast wireless charging and Wireless PowerShare.

Meanwhile, Google’s Pixel 10 Pro Fold packs a larger 5,015mAh battery with over 24 hours of typical usage and up to 84 hours using Extreme Battery Saver. It goes up to 50% in about 30 minutes using a 30W USB-C PPS charger. For wireless charging, I have tried Pixelsnap and other Qi2-certified chargers. Only up to 15W is supported.

Samsung’s lighter weight makes its battery capacity impressive, but Google’s larger battery and aggressive power management translate into longer endurance during everyday use.

Winner: Pixel 10 Pro Fold

Software experience and AI features: Samsung wants you to multitask, Google wants you to flow

Samsung and Google both offer excellent software, but they focus on different strengths.

The Galaxy Z Fold8 ships with Android 17 and One UI 9, optimized specifically for foldables. Features like multi-window support, two- and three-way split-screen, Galaxy AI, Now Nudge, Photo Assist, and Samsung’s productivity tools make it easy to get work done quickly. I’m looking forward to the My Fancam feature for subject-centered tracking shots from videos.

The Pixel 10 Pro Fold runs Android 16 with Google’s clean interface and promises seven years of OS, security, and Pixel Drop updates. It also includes exclusive Pixel AI experiences, enhanced Gemini integration like Gemini Live, Gemini Nano, etc., Satellite SOS, Call Assist, Live Translation, Pixel Screenshots, Magic Cue, and Google’s well-known photography tools.

Winner: Galaxy Z Fold8 for multitasking and productivity, while Pixel 10 Pro Fold for AI-powered everyday features and long-term software support.

Price and value

The Pixel 10 Pro Fold starts at $1,799, while Samsung’s newly announced Galaxy Z Fold8 starts at $1,899.99 and is currently available for pre-order.

Although Samsung costs about $100 more, the lighter design, Snapdragon processor, and foldable-specific productivity features help justify the premium. However, Google provides great value for money, offering better camera quality, 16GB RAM, IP68 protection, exclusive Android features, and seven years of software support.

Here’s how the official U.S. pricing compares across storage configurations:

The pricing difference becomes more noticeable as you move up the storage tiers. Samsung charges roughly $100 more for the base model, about $181 more for the 512GB version, and around $351 more for the 1TB model.

However, the good part is that if you pre-order the Fold8 now via Amazon, you get a $350 gift card bundled with the phone.

Winner: Pixel 10 Pro Fold

Who should buy the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8?

The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 is the better choice if you want your smartphone to replace your tablet or even your laptop for everyday tasks.

You should buy the Galaxy Z Fold8 if you:

  • Need a productivity-focused foldable. One UI offers some of the best multitasking features on any smartphone, including split-screen, floating windows, drag-and-drop between apps, and taskbar shortcuts.
  • Use your phone for work. The wider 4:3 inner display makes editing documents, spreadsheets, presentations, and emails much more comfortable.
  • Play graphics-intensive games. Powered by the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy, the Fold8 delivers stronger gaming performance and better sustained workloads than Google’s Tensor-powered alternative.
  • Already own Samsung devices. If you’re invested in the Galaxy ecosystem with a Galaxy Watch, Galaxy Buds, or Galaxy Tab, the Fold8 integrates seamlessly across devices.
  • Prefer a lighter foldable. At just 201 grams, it’s one of the lightest book-style foldables available, making it easier to carry and use throughout the day.
  • Create content regularly. Samsung’s Flex Mode, Dual Recording, and large inner display make recording and editing photos and videos more convenient.

In short, the Galaxy Z Fold8 is built for power users. If productivity, multitasking, and performance are your top priorities, it’s the foldable to beat.

Who should buy the Google Pixel 10 Pro Fold?

The Google Pixel 10 Pro Fold is ideal for buyers who want a premium foldable without sacrificing the signature Pixel experience.

Buy the Pixel 10 Pro Fold if you:

  • Take lots of photos. After multiple tests, I can say Google produces some of the best smartphone photos, especially in challenging lighting conditions.
  • Want the smartest AI features. Built-in Gemini integration, Pixel-exclusive AI tools, Call Assist, and other intelligent features make everyday tasks simpler.
  • Prefer clean Android. Pixel delivers Google’s vision of Android without additional software layers, resulting in a streamlined user experience.
  • Value long software support. Google promises seven years of Android OS, security, and Pixel Drop updates, helping the phone stay relevant for years.
  • Need a more durable foldable. With IP68 dust and water resistance, the Pixel offers stronger protection against the elements than most foldable phones.
  • Want better value. Starting at $1,799, the Pixel 10 Pro Fold costs less than Samsung’s Fold8 while still delivering flagship hardware and premium features.

If cameras, AI, software longevity, and overall value matter more than multitasking performance, the Pixel 10 Pro Fold is the smarter purchase.

Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 vs Google Pixel 10 Pro Fold: Which is best foldable phone?

Samsung and Google have both pushed foldable smartphones forward, but they’ve done so in different ways.

The Galaxy Z Fold8 refines the traditional foldable formula with a lighter design, a more powerful Snapdragon processor, improved multitasking, and software that makes full use of the large inner display. It’s the phone I’d recommend to professionals, power users, gamers, and anyone who wants a foldable that can genuinely replace multiple devices.

The Pixel 10 Pro Fold, on the other hand, proves that foldables don’t have to compromise on cameras or software. Google’s combination of excellent computational photography, AI-powered features, IP68 protection, and seven years of updates makes it one of the most well-rounded foldables available today.

Ultimately, there’s no single winner because these phones are designed for different audiences. Which foldable are you choosing? Let me know in the comments below!

mainEntity.name: Is there a lightweight alternative to Adobe Acrobat for Windows?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. All four tools tested here are built as smaller, faster alternatives to Acrobat. PDNob comes closest to matching Acrobat's editing depth while staying under 600MB installed, and PDF-XChange Editor covers most of Acrobat's day-to-day functions in a portable build with no installer at all.

mainEntity.name: Is a portable PDF editor safer or more private than an installed one?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Photographic Styles are designed for still photos and do not affect video recordings. Portability and privacy are separate things. A portable app like PDF-XChange Editor Portable avoids leaving an installation footprint on a shared PC, but it still processes files locally the same way an installed editor does. For actual data privacy, a self-hosted option like Stirling-PDF is the stronger choice since files never leave your own server.

mainEntity.name: Is there an open-source lightweight PDF editor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Xournal++ and Stirling-PDF are both open-source in this test. Xournal++ is a lightweight desktop app built for annotation, while Stirling-PDF is a self-hosted, browser-based tool with 60+ PDF operations that keeps every file on your own hardware.

title.rendered: Epic 4K Gojo Satoru wallpapers for iPhone every Jujutsu Kaisen fan should download

content.rendered:
If you’re an otaku like me, your iPhone wallpaper changes as new anime releases. But every time I switch away from Gojo Satoru, I somehow end up coming right back. His iconic white hair, glowing blue eyes, and unforgettable moments from Jujutsu Kaisen make him a sensation.

Here, I have handpicked the best 4K Gojo Satoru wallpapers for iPhone Lock Screen and Home Screen setups. Some wallpapers capture Gojo’s playful personality, while others showcase his overwhelming power with stunning purple energy. Explore the collection and download your favorite one for free.

1. Gojo sitting in a sunlit classroom  

The very first wallpaper captures something fans don’t see often: Gojo simply relaxing in class on a nice summer day. I like how the bright blue sky complements his white hair, while the open window instantly brightens your screen.

If you like colorful summer aesthetic wallpapers for iPhone, this is easily one of the strongest choices.

Download

2. Minimal Gojo wallpaper that’s perfect for every iPhone 

Sometimes less is more. This close-up portrait focuses entirely on Gojo’s face while he casually flashes a peace sign. The neutral background makes him stand out and keeps widgets and app icons highly visible. It’s one of my favorite minimal iPhone wallpapers. 

Download

3. Gojo Satoru: The king of Jujutsu High 

If you’re searching for dark Gojo wallpapers for iPhone, download this one. Instead of Gojo’s playful personality, it presents him as an untouchable king of the Jujutsu world. So cool!

I am excited to see him break off the Prism Realm and finally face Sukuna in the next Jujutsu Kaisen season. What do you think about that battle?

Also read: Netflix’s 2026 anime lineup looks big, but these are the ones I’d watch

Download

4. Gojo with his limitless Purple technique 

Few wallpapersrepresentGojo’s overwhelming strength better than this one. Floating among glowing purple symbols, Gojo appears as the strongest sorcererwith hisSixEyes revealed. The cinematic effects make my screen actually stand out in public.

Download

5. Gojo arrives at Shibuya station 

I can never forget Shibuya station as it’s the starting point of Kenjaku’s masterplan of the Culling Game. In the wallpaper, you get Gojo inside a crowded Shibuya subway station with his blindfold partially raised.

Fans looking for authentic Jujutsu Kaisen iPhone wallpapers will appreciate this one.

Download

6. Lawson convenience store walk 

One of my favorite things about Gojo is how effortlessly cool he looks doing absolutely normal things. This wallpaper captures him walking outside a convenience store with a drink in hand. It’s giving strong slice-of-life anime vibes. 

Download

7. Gojo’s carefree summer look  

There are plenty of action-packed Gojo wallpapers out there, but I like this one more because it captures his playful personality.  

Looking up toward a bright blue sky while casually tossing a piece of candy into the air, Gojo looks completely carefree. His presence reminds fans why he’s one of the most charismatic characters in Jujutsu Kaisen.

Download

8. Classic Gojo blindfold smile 

Not all wallpapers require special effects to become iconic. This portrait is a good example.  

Gojo stands confidently wearing his signature blindfold with a calm smile. The clean white background keeps the focus entirely on him, making this one of the most timeless Gojo wallpaper iPhone choices in the collection. 

Download

9. Gojo’s brilliant blue eyes steal the show  

Gojo Satoru’s Six Eyes is itself a plot in Jujutsu Kaisen, and this crisp wallpaper makes sure they’re impossible to ignore. The close-up portrait highlights his glowing blue eyes peeking over his sunglasses while his hand casually runs through his white hair.  

Download

10. Pointing Straight at You 

This wallpaper instantly feels interactive. Instead of posing naturally, Gojo points directly toward you with a confident grin. Whenever I am out with friends, I set up this Lock Screen wallpaper as if Gojo is watching anyone touch my phone. The perspective adds depth and makes the wallpaper feel more dynamic than traditional anime wallpapers.  

Download

11. Gojo watching over Tokyo 

Confidence defines this wallpaper. Gojo sits casually on the edge of a rooftop overlooking the city skyline. The low-angle perspective makes him appear larger than life, perfectly matching his status as the strongest sorcerer.

For anyone who enjoys cinematic Depth Effect wallpaper, this is one of the strongest choices.

Download

12. Cinematic Gojo Satoru cool pose  

This is definitely one of my favorite wallpapers of Gojo sensei as it perfectly describes his calm attitude and style. The cinematic lighting, iconic sunglasses, and relaxed pose give it a clean yet powerful look for everyday use.

Download

13. Ultimate Gojo Satoru Hollow Purple wallpaper 

If there’s one wallpaper that perfectly represents Gojo’s Limitless power, it’s this one. Gojo has unleashed his Blue and Red to create Hollow Purple with one hand extended as if he’s controlling the entire battlefield. The swirling cosmic effects and glowing lightning make the wallpaper most visually striking. 

Download

14. Gojo: Defender of the Void barrier 

Another incredible dark wallpaper. Gojo stands calmly in side profile while rocks and debris appear frozen around him, showcasing the unstoppable force of his Infinity technique. Even when surrounded by chaos, he remains completely unshaken.

Download

15. Gojo Satoru Purple aura wallpaper 

Gojo and his undefeated aura are a big reason behind JJK fandom. Standing with his hands in his pockets, Gojo is surrounded by swirling purple energy that creates a mysterious atmosphere. Every time I glance at my Lock Screen, it’s like watching calm before a legendary fight.

Download

16. Gojo enjoying rooftop sunset with sweet treats

Gojo isn’t always fighting curses. Sometimes he simply enjoys dessert while watching the sunset. Fans know Gojo has a serious sweet tooth, and this golden hour wallpaper celebrates that fun side of his personality.

Download

17. Peaceful Gojo wallpaper bringing Zen energy 

The next wallpaper is something totally different. Instead of action or confidence, it focuses on silence. Gojo sits cross-legged inside a room while golden sunlight pours through the window. His silhouette dominates the foreground, creating a spiritual atmosphere.

Download

18. Evening stroll with Gojo 

I feel like this wallpaper is telling me that Gojo is inviting me to follow him into the next adventure. The warm sunlight stretches across the road while the glowing skyline creates a cinematic backdrop that feels almost like the ending scene of an anime movie or manga.

Download

19. Gojo’s Limitless Awakening 

Saved the most powerful wallpaper for last. Gojo lifts his blindfold as brilliant blue eyes illuminate the surrounding darkness. Every detail, from his confident smile to the glowing reflections, presents Gojo at his absolute strongest.

If you only download one wallpaper from this collection, this is the one I’d recommend.

Download

Why Gojo wallpapers look so good on iPhone

Unlike many anime wallpapers that feel cluttered, Gojo wallpapers usually have portrait orientation and leave plenty of breathing room around the subject. That makes widgets, clocks, and notifications easier to read without covering the artwork.

Most images in this collection are optimized in high-resolution to look sharp on modern iPhones.

Final thoughts

Gojo Satoru has no shortage of unforgettable moments, but I curated the best wallpapers that capture more than just his strength—they showcase his personality. From carefree summer scenes and casual city walks to cosmic battles and iconic blindfold reveals, this collection offers something for every Jujutsu Kaisen fan.

So, save your favorites, switch them with the seasons or your mood, and let Gojo’s iconic presence make every unlock feel a little more epic. For more amazing wallpapers, don’t forget to check out the CrestWall app!

mainEntity.name: Is a portable PDF editor safer or more private than an installed one?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Photographic Styles are designed for still photos and do not affect video recordings. Portability and privacy are separate things. title.rendered: Apple could become the No. 2 foldable phone brand in 2026

content.rendered:
Apple could capture 25% of global foldable smartphone shipments in 2026 and enter the category in second place, according to a new Counterpoint Research forecast. That would put it behind Samsung at 32% and just ahead of Huawei at 24%.

The ranking is a projection, not a sales result. Apple still has not announced a foldable iPhone, and any launch details remain unofficial.

Apple could take one in four foldable shipments

Counterpoint expects global foldable phone shipments to grow 21% year over year in 2026. Apple’s possible arrival, stronger competition, and continued demand for premium book-style models are expected to drive that growth.

Here is how the research firm sees the market splitting this year:

Samsung would remain the leader, though its share is forecast to fall from 40% in 2025. Apple would land only one percentage point ahead of Huawei, so the fight for second place could be much closer than the headline suggests.

The forecast depends on an unannounced iPhone

Reports around Apple’s first foldable iPhone point to a book-style device that could arrive later in 2026. None of that has been confirmed by Apple.

Counterpoint believes larger foldable screens will become more useful as phone-based AI expands into document summaries, editing, scheduling, and tasks that move between apps. A wider inner display gives those tools more room to show content and controls together.

Samsung already has the advantage of a mature product line, retail reach, and years of foldable software experience. Its newly announced Galaxy Z Fold8 lineup also gives buyers more wide-screen options before Apple’s expected entry.

Apple does not need to overtake Samsung for its first foldable to reshape the market. Capturing anything close to the forecast 25% share would immediately make it a major competitor—but the actual result will depend on the phone arriving on time and convincing buyers at what is expected to be a premium price.

Unlock more with Apple:

  • AirPods 5 Wireless Earbuds
  • Apple HomeView
  • Apple TV 4K (4th gen)
  • MacBook Neo 13-inch Laptop
  • iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)
  • MacBook Air 13-inch Laptop with M5 chip

mainEntity.name: Is there a lightweight alternative to Adobe Acrobat for Windows?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. All four tools tested here are built as smaller, faster alternatives to Acrobat. PDNob comes closest to matching Acrobat's editing depth while staying under 600MB installed, and PDF-XChange Editor covers most of Acrobat's day-to-day functions in a portable build with no installer at all.

mainEntity.name: Is a portable PDF editor safer or more private than an installed one?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Photographic Styles are designed for still photos and do not affect video recordings. Portability and privacy are separate things. A portable app like PDF-XChange Editor Portable avoids leaving an installation footprint on a shared PC, but it still processes files locally the same way an installed editor does. For actual data privacy, a self-hosted option like Stirling-PDF is the stronger choice since files never leave your own server.

mainEntity.name: Is there an open-source lightweight PDF editor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Xournal++ and Stirling-PDF are both open-source in this test. Xournal++ is a lightweight desktop app built for annotation, while Stirling-PDF is a self-hosted, browser-based tool with 60+ PDF operations that keeps every file on your own hardware.

mainEntity.name: How many times has Simpsons collaborated with Fortnite before?

acceptedAnswer.text: So far, only one Fortnite x Simpsons collab has been released. It came out in November 2025.

mainEntity.name: Which was the most popular thing about the previous Fortnite x Simpsons collab?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Springfield Island map was arguably the most well-received addition and hence the most popular thing to emerge out of the collab.

acceptedAnswer.text: Plenty of different shows from that category, including South Park, Family Guy, and Rick & Morty, have previously collaborated with Fortnite.

title.rendered: Geekbench 7 introduces new CPU and GPU tests across AI, gaming, and media

content.rendered:
Primate Labs has launched Geekbench 7, the latest version of its benchmarking tool for smartphones, tablets, PCs, and Macs. The update brings new CPU and GPU tests focused on AI, gaming, media processing, and content creation, while also changing how the benchmark measures multi-core performance.

Geekbench 7 arrives more than three years after Geekbench 6. During that time, on-device AI features, photo and video editing, and graphics-heavy apps have become far more common, so Primate Labs has updated many of the workloads used to measure device performance.

Geekbench 7 adds new AI, GPU, and media workloads

One of the biggest changes in Geekbench 7 is its updated GPU Benchmark, which now places greater emphasis on machine learning and content creation. The updated GPU Benchmark includes workloads based on face tracking for live video filters, AI image upscaling, virtual backgrounds in video calls, RAW image processing, video color grading, path tracing, and fluid simulation.

The update also adds support for Nvidia CUDA, joining existing GPU APIs including OpenCL, Vulkan, and Apple’s Metal.

The CPU benchmark now includes workloads for AV1 video encoding, Opus audio compression, and video playback with live captions generated using OpenAI’s Whisper speech recognition model. Primate Labs has also expanded the datasets used across several benchmarks, including file compression, PDF viewing, software development, and image-processing tests, to better reflect how today’s apps and software are used.

Multi-core testing has been updated

Geekbench 7 also changes how it measures multi-core performance. Instead of treating every workload as multi-threaded, Geekbench 7 now only uses multiple threads when the real-world task would actually benefit from them. As an example, Primate Labs says the HTML5 Browser test has been removed from the multi-core suite because web browsing is generally single-threaded or only lightly threaded.

Geekbench 7 is available starting today. The standard version remains free for personal use, while Geekbench 7 Pro is available at a 20% discount through August 6 as part of the launch promotion.

Have you tried Geekbench 7 yet? Let us know how it performs on your device in the comments.

mainEntity.name: Is there a lightweight alternative to Adobe Acrobat for Windows?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. All four tools tested here are built as smaller, faster alternatives to Acrobat. PDNob comes closest to matching Acrobat's editing depth while staying under 600MB installed, and PDF-XChange Editor covers most of Acrobat's day-to-day functions in a portable build with no installer at all.

mainEntity.name: Is a portable PDF editor safer or more private than an installed one?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Photographic Styles are designed for still photos and do not affect video recordings. Portability and privacy are separate things. A portable app like PDF-XChange Editor Portable avoids leaving an installation footprint on a shared PC, but it still processes files locally the same way an installed editor does. For actual data privacy, a self-hosted option like Stirling-PDF is the stronger choice since files never leave your own server.

mainEntity.name: Is there an open-source lightweight PDF editor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Xournal++ and Stirling-PDF are both open-source in this test. Xournal++ is a lightweight desktop app built for annotation, while Stirling-PDF is a self-hosted, browser-based tool with 60+ PDF operations that keeps every file on your own hardware.

Experience

title.rendered: Apple’s OpenAI trade-secret lawsuit gets a new district judge

content.rendered:
Apple’s trade-secret lawsuit against OpenAI has been reassigned to U.S. District Judge Edward Davila, replacing the magistrate judge initially assigned to the case.

The change puts a district judge in charge as both sides prepare for discovery and early case deadlines. Magistrate Judge Nathanael Cousins will handle discovery matters.

Why the judge changed

When Apple filed the lawsuit on July 10, the case was randomly assigned to Magistrate Judge Virginia K. DeMarchi.

The court’s initial scheduling order required every party to say whether it consented to DeMarchi overseeing the full case. Unlike a district judge, a magistrate judge needs consent from all parties to run a federal civil case through trial and judgment.

Apple filed its consent-or-declination form shortly before the reassignment. 9to5Mac reports that Apple appears to have declined magistrate jurisdiction, although the form itself is not public.

The October hearing needs a new date

The initial case management conference scheduled for October 13 before Judge DeMarchi has been vacated. Judge Davila will set a replacement date.

Other early deadlines remain on the current schedule. The parties are due to discuss settlement options, evidence exchange, and their discovery plan by September 22. Initial disclosures and a joint case management statement are due October 6.

Nothing has been decided yet

The reassignment is procedural. Judge Davila has not ruled on Apple’s allegations, and the court has not granted an injunction against OpenAI.

Apple alleges in its 41-page complaint that OpenAI and former Apple employees used confidential hardware information to support the AI company’s device business. OpenAI has rejected that account, and its broader response says it is not aware of evidence that Apple’s claims have merit.

Judge Davila will now handle major motions and decide the case unless it settles or is otherwise resolved. Cousins will oversee discovery disputes, where both sides may fight over what evidence must be shared.

That stage could matter more to OpenAI’s hardware team than the judge change itself. Apple’s requested injunction has not been granted, but a future order restricting disputed information could still slow OpenAI’s device plans.

  • AirPods 5 Wireless Earbuds
  • Apple HomeView
  • Apple TV 4K (4th gen)
  • MacBook Neo 13-inch Laptop
  • iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)
  • MacBook Air 13-inch Laptop with M5 chip

mainEntity.name: Is there a lightweight alternative to Adobe Acrobat for Windows?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. All four tools tested here are built as smaller, faster alternatives to Acrobat. PDNob comes closest to matching Acrobat's editing depth while staying under 600MB installed, and PDF-XChange Editor covers most of Acrobat's day-to-day functions in a portable build with no installer at all.

mainEntity.name: Is a portable PDF editor safer or more private than an installed one?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Photographic Styles are designed for still photos and do not affect video recordings. Portability and privacy are separate things. A portable app like PDF-XChange Editor Portable avoids leaving an installation footprint on a shared PC, but it still processes files locally the same way an installed editor does. For actual data privacy, a self-hosted option like Stirling-PDF is the stronger choice since files never leave your own server.

mainEntity.name: Is there an open-source lightweight PDF editor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Xournal++ and Stirling-PDF are both open-source in this test. Xournal++ is a lightweight desktop app built for annotation, while Stirling-PDF is a self-hosted, browser-based tool with 60+ PDF operations that keeps every file on your own hardware.

title.rendered: ChatGPT can now connect to your Apple Health data in the U.S.

content.rendered:
OpenAI is rolling out Health in ChatGPT to eligible users in the United States, bringing Apple Health and supported medical records into the AI chatbot. The feature, which was previously available only to a limited group of beta testers, is now launching for users on the web and iOS across Free, Go, Plus, and Pro plans.

ChatGPT can use your health data to provide personalized answers

With your permission, ChatGPT can access information you’ve connected through Apple Health and supported medical records. That can include medications, lab results, recent doctor visits, sleep data, activity, and workouts.

Beyond answering general health questions, the Health section can also help users make sense of their own data. It can compare lab results from different dates, highlight what has changed since a previous appointment, keep track of medications, and bring together information from sleep, activity, and workouts to help users better understand overall health trends.

You can also ask follow-up questions, add details that aren’t in your connected records, or correct outdated information, and ChatGPT will use those updates throughout the conversation.

Your health data isn’t used to train ChatGPT

OpenAI says information connected through Apple Health and supported medical records isn’t used to train its AI models or serve advertisements. Conversations that rely on this information are also excluded from model training.

ChatGPT asks for your permission before accessing any connected or shared health information. Users can also continue using the Health section without linking medical records or Apple Health, allowing them to ask general health questions without sharing personal data.

Health in ChatGPT is rolling out today to logged-in users in the United States who are 18 or older on the web and iOS.

Would you connect Apple Health to ChatGPT? Let us know in the comments below.

  • Apple HomeView
  • Apple TV 4K (4th gen)
  • MacBook Neo 13-inch Laptop

  • MacBook Air 13-inch Laptop with M5 chip

mainEntity.name: Is there a lightweight alternative to Adobe Acrobat for Windows?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. All four tools tested here are built as smaller, faster alternatives to Acrobat. PDNob comes closest to matching Acrobat's editing depth while staying under 600MB installed, and PDF-XChange Editor covers most of Acrobat's day-to-day functions in a portable build with no installer at all.

mainEntity.name: Is a portable PDF editor safer or more private than an installed one?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Photographic Styles are designed for still photos and do not affect video recordings. Portability and privacy are separate things. A portable app like PDF-XChange Editor Portable avoids leaving an installation footprint on a shared PC, but it still processes files locally the same way an installed editor does. For actual data privacy, a self-hosted option like Stirling-PDF is the stronger choice since files never leave your own server.

mainEntity.name: Is there an open-source lightweight PDF editor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Xournal++ and Stirling-PDF are both open-source in this test. Xournal++ is a lightweight desktop app built for annotation, while Stirling-PDF is a self-hosted, browser-based tool with 60+ PDF operations that keeps every file on your own hardware.

aioseo_head_json.author_bio:
Vikhyat has a bachelor’s degree in Electronic and Communication Engineering and over five years of writing experience. His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. 

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.
